#1890. Mauricio Pochettino's Man United SQUAD AUDIT: Axe EIGHT stars, new role for the attacker he's 'always liked' and who could be his new Dele Alli... now give YOUR player-by-player verdict

Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:11 EST, 14 November 2026

Walking into a club in turmoil is nothing new for Mauricio Pochettino.

He arrived at Southampton with the Saints three points clear of the relegation zone. Tottenham Hotspur were crying out for some leadership after Andre Villas-Boas and Tim Sherwood's spells, while Chelsea picked up Pochettino in 2023 on the back of their lowest league finish for more than 25 years.

Now it's Manchester United that require what Victor Wanyama once described as Pochettino's 'magic touch' – and they need it quick as they sit in the relegation zone with ten games played. Pochettino remains weeks removed from the January transfer window and has a number of first-team regulars out with long-term injuries, so his reputation of improving the players at his disposal will be put to the test.

He has developed a reputation for placing faith in youth – while at Tottenham, Pochettino handed 12 debuts to players aged 21 or under, more than any other manager.

Money will be tight and United look almost certain to miss out on next season's Champions League, which will make squad development significantly harder, so Pochettino will have to make do and mend with a lot of the current underperforming crop of players.

With all that in mind, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over the 36 players Pochettino will be inheriting when he walks through the door at Carrington next week.

And you can scroll to the end of the article to have your say on who should stay, and who should go...

Mauricio Pochettino will rapidly have to assess which Man United players to discard

Lammens won't be going anywhere. He is United's No 1 and despite a downturn in form this season, he's not become a bad goalkeeper overnight. Pochettino's trusted goalkeeping coach Toni Jimenez will almost certainly replace Craig Mawson to bring some fresh ideas.

Jimenez focuses a lot on developing goalkeepers to be comfortable as sweepers and playing higher up. That is a sore spot in Lammens' game – recently exposed by Bournemouth striker Evanilson – but proper coaching should help develop Lammens, just like Jimenez developed Hugo Lloris.

A summer arrival from Leeds United as a back-up goalkeeper. Pochettino has more important issues than messing around with his No2.

Heaton is hugely popular at the club and while he doesn't play, he is viewed as a vital cog in the dressing room given his wealth of experience. He turns 41 later this season and has been busy preparing for life away from the pitch.

Heaton has completed courses on becoming a sporting director, as well as an executive leadership short course from Oxford University.

He also holds his goalkeeper coach B-Licence, A-Licence outfield, and a certificate of football management from UEFA.

Pochettino would be wise to keep Heaton in-house, even if not as a player. He is a respected figure who knows United inside out and that shouldn't be overlooked as Pochettino tries to build out a culture.

Senne Lammens (right) has made a shaky start to the season but will be going nowhere

Dalot is highly respected by every manager that works with him for the effort he puts in, something that can't always be said of some of his team-mates.

But he is woefully short of the required quality to take United forward and he is not a comfortable fit for Pochettino's ideals, either.

Pochettino gets width in his sides via the full backs and that requires a relentless runner – which Dalot is – having quality both defensively and in attack, which Dalot does not.

Malo Gusto, who is keen to leave Chelsea and could become a key target for United, spoke of how Pochettino developed his game in 2024 when he said: 'He helps us a lot. He has tried to show us the desire to win, to keep fighting against every team.

'He talks to us a lot about tactics, technique and everything. He is a good person as well. He tries to help us a lot on the pitch and off it. He is a good coach for this young team.

'He is here for this. He knows he has to wake up our mentality, to wake up our desire to win everything.'

United have neglected their back-line for years and it's time for a dramatic refresh, starting with shifting Dalot, who is under contract until 2028.

It is time for Man United to move on from Diogo Dalot - he is short of the quality required

Dalot has at least shown he has the engine to get up and down, which could offer a lifeline under Pochettino, but Mazraoui hasn't.

Full backs are essential to Pochettino's high-intensity, high press 4-2-3-1, and that's not a formula that suits Mazraoui's abilities.

Privately, sources close to the dressing room have suggested in recent weeks that Mazraoui, another under contract until 2028, is keen for a new challenge.

Overhauling the defence is one of the main topics of conversation among agents and players right now but De Ligt's future is secure at Old Trafford.

He is under contract until 2029, with the option of a further year, and many figures behind the scenes believe he can bounce back from such a long period out with injury to be a success.

De Ligt's injury record, as well as the fact he isn't a natural fit for Pochettino's idea of the perfect, mobile centre back, makes him an intriguing prospect.

Strong in physical duels, he could become a key squad player.

Maguire has taken more criticism than most during his time at United and deserves credit for how he has overcome it.

His contract expires in the summer, with the option of a further year, and Maguire has described playing for United as the 'ultimate honour' so is unlikely to agitate to leave.

That being said, Pochettino puts a lot of emphasis on recovery pace given the high line he has favoured in the past and the Argentine's tactics have routinely exposed centre backs in transition, with speed essential to masking shortcomings.

Maguire would undoubtedly struggle in that department and while his physical profile would appeal, he said earlier this year that he does not want to be kept around for 'sentimental value'.

'I love this club. But it's got to be right for myself, it's got to be right for the club as well,' Maguire said in March before a one-year extension was triggered.

'I don't want to be staying on sentimental value. I want to be staying because I want to be there and the club want me to drive the club forward still, and they feel like I've got a big part to play in it.'

The prospect of a diminishing role, with United planning multiple defensive reinforcements, may see both sides agree it's time for a change.

After seven years it may be time for Harry Maguire to move on, with his contract expiring

A player that looks to have one foot out the door after calling out director of football Jason Wilcox following the defeat by Atletico Madrid.

It's funny, almost, given Pochettino's arrival should suit Martinez down to the ground. In theory, he is the exact type of player his compatriot would implore his bosses to recruit.

Pochettino puts huge emphasis on passing out from the back and Martinez is the best in that category among United's centre backs.

Pochettino is also incredibly intense, something Martinez has been for some time at United, sometimes to the group's benefit and sometimes to its detriment.

The Argentine's contract expires in the summer and while there is an option to trigger a further year to avoid a World Cup winner walking away for nothing, the expectation is that he won't agree to a new one and his time at United is more likely than not drawing to a close.

He holds a desire to play in Spain and that may not vanish overnight. But if anyone can connect with Martinez about a longer-term role, it's a fellow Argentine.

Has the potential to be the biggest winner of the Pochettino appointment.

Pochettino's full-back-turned-winger style totally plays into Dorgu's hands given both his engine and his comfort playing higher up the pitch. Look at the development of Danny Rose – who played more games for Pochettino than any other player – and Kyle Walker, as well as Sergino Dest with the USA.

Dorgu has a lot of the attributes Pochettino craves while he also remains raw enough that intense, but targeted, coaching could improve him.

He should immediately become one of Pochettino's go-to men.

Where there are concerns around Maguire's ability to play in a system which squeezes everyone that bit higher up the pitch, Yoro should thrive.

He showed against Villa, with a chase down to deny Nicolas Jackson a run on goal, that he possesses the necessary recovery pace.

Pochettino's centre backs need to be strong passers and Yoro can improve in this area, although he has shown a willingness to dictate with long diagonals, as well as burst through lines as a ball-carrier.

United need five reliable centre backs in the squad moving forward and Yoro can establish himself as the No1.

Given Pochettino's track record with young players, he should be really excited at becoming a key piece of the puzzle under him.

A reunion… but one that may not last very long.

In a 2017 book about Pochettino, Shaw revealed his desire to work under him again and that wish has now come true.

'With Southampton he achieved the impossible,' said Shaw. 'We were one of the best footballing teams in the league... I do hope that I can play for him again one day. And I think he really wants me to play under him again.'

Pochettino used to call Shaw his 'son' and their relationship has stayed strong over the years.

But Pochettino is also a winner and will be acutely aware that Shaw cannot maintain the levels that Pochettino will require from his full backs after years of injury problems.

Sources close to the player have suggested the potential for a one-year extension given the relationship with Pochettino, even if those same sources believe the time is right for a fresh start.

A long servant but not one that can take United forward from this lowest of ebbs.

Luke Shaw and Pochettino enjoyed success together at Southampton but the reunion won't last long

Arriving as an Ineos project, United aren't going to cut their losses on Heaven just yet.

His strong passing ability will appeal to Pochettino and his coaches and he's worth a season of proper coaching to see how high or low his ceiling is.

Heaven can be reckless, particularly in his approach to tackling, but he's got a good physical profile and those who have worked with him have praised his approach to training and willingness to listen to coaches.

United are likely to go out and sign two new centre backs in the summer – at least they hope to – but Heaven should get a shot at development as a bit-part player.

Wholly ignored despite a left back crisis this season, Amass is widely expected to be out the door in January.

It is hard to blame him, either, given United's decision to keep him around has stunted his development.

Amass is a strong crosser of the ball and, in time, could develop into a full back in Pochettino's vision.

But neither Amass nor Pochettino will have time to wait and see. With a left back high on the shopping list, to go with Dorgu's expected ascension, this relationship shouldn't last too long.

Kamason has played both at right back and right wing for United's Under 21s and that plays massively into his hands in a bid to try and catch the eye of his new manager.

The United youngster is a well-rounded full back that constantly looks to get forward, all while not neglecting his defensive responsibilities.

Kamason has trained regularly with the first team in recent months and that could be a sign of things to come under Pochettino, too.

United rolled the dice on Leon a year ago in a deal worth an initial £3.3million – but the move has not worked out at all.

The 19-year-old hasn't come close to making a first-team appearance and his agent has even suggested they are getting itchy feet despite sub-par performances for United's Under 21s.

'If there isn't a plan to break into the first team between December and January, we'll look for a way out for him,' Leon's representative Renato Bittar admitted. 'A loan somewhere where he can compete, get playing time, and return to Manchester.'

Having observed the academy teams closer than most in recent seasons, Leon hasn't shown anywhere near enough to merit becoming a project player for Pochettino.

Mount left for United in the same summer Pochettino was hired by Chelsea, so their crossover was minimal.

How much say Pochettino had in that decision remains unclear, perhaps it was insignificant, but now they will finally work together.

Mount feels disposable, not least because he hasn't registered a single assist in the Premier League for United since joining in 2023 for £60million.

With so many options ahead of him in those inverted winger roles, and with Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans preferred as No 10s, Mount needs shifting.

Contract talks have stalled in recent weeks and months but an ambitious new manager could swing momentum back towards reigning Player of the Year Fernandes staying at Old Trafford.

The way Pochettino platformed Christian Eriksen and Dele Alli at Tottenham, as well as Cole Palmer at Chelsea, suggests Fernandes will get the role he needs to be at his very best.

Fernandes' mobility, and ability to run beyond his centre forward, is a strength, as is his vision to supply team-mates in open play and at set-pieces. If Fernandes plays well, so do United, generally. Pochettino favours inverted attackers, so Fernandes could even start off the left if his manager wanted to position Matheus Cunha or Tielemans more centrally.

'He's given me the freedom to play my stuff and I like it when he frees you because I feel I can express my stuff more,' Palmer said of Pochettino's coaching back in 2024.

'I'm loving it. Every day he's talking to you about different things, not just football things but life things as well. He's good at making you feel good and trying to get the best out of you.'

Pochettino's free-flowing approach could be exactly what is needed to keep Bruno Fernandes

Pochettino knows all about Santos having worked with him at Chelsea when he was a teenager still finding his way.

The reports at that time, during a pre-season tour in North Carolina and Philadelphia, were that Santos' profile appealed to Pochettino, only for the club to go ahead and sanction loan moves to Nottingham Forest and then Strasbourg.

Santos is a summer arrival for £50m and will get more time to find his role in this United side.

He has enough talent to become a reliable deputy to Baleba as the deep-lying midfielder when everyone is fully fit.

Tielemans is a high-IQ player that signed a five-year contract in the summer so, truthfully, won't be going anywhere.

That being said, Tielemans' running power isn't there and the demands of a Pochettino system, if he is still the same coach that bowed out at Chelsea, may make that secondary midfield role difficult.

It feels like Tielemans could be a specialist player that Pochettino uses in games where his side expect to dominate possession.

Tielemans' composure on the ball is superior to that of many of his team-mates and that's not a trait Pochettino will overlook quickly, even if he reportedly had reservations on a younger Tielemans when he was managing at Tottenham.

A big winner. The £70m summer signing needs to be used in the correct way to realise his potential and Pochettino's track record should be music to Baleba's ears.

Pochettino has typically liked one of his central midfielders to drop deep in possession to create a back three – see Eric Dier at Tottenham – and Baleba should be comfortable fulfilling that role.

Moises Caicedo and Wanyama are two other success stories in the deeper No6 role that Baleba should now thrive in under Pochettino's watch, with his combativeness and tackling making him a natural fit.

'Tactically, he has taught me a lot,' Wanyama previously said of Pochettino.

'Before, I was just thinking, "I'll just sit here and defend". But if you're playing for him, it's not only defending. You have to attack also. You have to know the right time. I have learned so much from him.'

Now it's time for Baleba to study up and take his game to the next level.

Carlos Baleba has a had a slow start to life at United but a managerial change could unlock his potential

It transpired that Pochettino wanted to make Ugarte his first signing at Chelsea, only for United to get in ahead of them for the Uruguayan.

Ugarte was all set to leave United in the summer were it not for a serious injury at the World Cup that left him sidelined for months.

Pochettino liked the profile of player he saw when Ugarte was scouted at Sporting Lisbon but he looks a different, far less effective, player in England.

Minds appear to be made up upstairs when it comes to moving on from Ugarte.

Where Baleba will need to drop deep, the other midfielder in Pochettino's system is the one who is expected to drive and bypass midfield blocks.

Pochettino will be acutely aware that Mainoo is extremely popular among United fans and while athleticism is often levelled against him as a weak point in his game, Pochettino will need to find a way of improving that while also nurturing his many talents.

Tottenham's Mousa Dembele was moulded by Pochettino from an attacking midfielder into a deep-lying controller, urged to dribble to break lines and open up the game.

Mainoo has many similar traits to others Pochettino has worked with, such as Weston McKennie with the US national team.

'They will get pushed in training more than the games they will be playing. It is all a mental thing,' former Southampton striker Rickie Lambert once said.

If Mainoo can come through the initial boot camp, he can flourish.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of United's top talents and will stay but has to improve his physicality

A better player than people give him credit for but one that really needs to put a full season together at first-team level to see where he is at.

That won't be under Pochettino at United but United, if they really believe he can be part of their future, need to find Fletcher a loan move where he can feature in 35-40 games.

Clubs in League One would be all over him.

The deep-lying midfielder that can drop in to form a back three is fundamental to how Pochettino wants to play and that's a style that would suit Tyler Fletcher, rather than the more attacking Jack.

Again, figures at United and up in Scotland, just want to see Fletcher get a run of games under his belt.

Kilmarnock wanted him in the summer, but United wanted to keep Fletcher in house.

If Pochettino and United really care about his career, he should be one of the first out the door on loan in January.

Senior academy figures are the most excited about Thwaites' potential, even if it would be unfair to expect him to make a big impact on the first team in the near future.

Technically his level is particularly high, a European pass-first, press-resistant game that will appeal to Pochettino and his coaches.

But physically there is a way to go, which should mean Thwaites is kept around as a project player.

Brought in as an Ineos project piece, after two mediocre loan spells in Switzerland with Lausanne, it's time to have Kone come back into the building and put him to work with a relentless coach like Pochettino.

Kone's twitchy game-style and desire to break through lines makes him something of a hybrid of players Pochettino has coached in the past.

Having watched him up close in the academy set-up before he went out on loan, and spoken to those who coached Kone then, it would be a big gamble for Pochettino to put his trust in him.

But Kone's ceiling feels sky high. It's time to see if he can go into the lab and come out as a Dembele-Wanyama hybrid.

Physically he has an advanced profile for his age but United have long preached that they want to take things slow as Orozco settles into life in England and gets a grip of the language.

He is neat and tidy on the ball and has shown an ability to zip passes through the lines but not enough to suggest an elevation to the first-team group.

Academy football doesn't develop players quickly enough so a carefully selected loan move, perhaps in a technical league like the Netherlands or Belgium, would be ideal.

He needs to look at how Pochettino used players like Lucas Moura and Eriksen in the past to see how he can take his game to the next level.

Cunha has a swagger about him that United like and while he was better suited to Ruben Amorim's system than he was Michael Carrick's, Pochettino's preference for narrow wide players, funnelling them into central areas while full backs create the width, means this managerial shift should play into his hands.

'Cunha is a maverick who does things that are hard to find in some players,' Amorim once said of the Brazilian.

'He plays with the ball, but he has an aura that can do something to the opponent's heads. And that is really important.'

It was recently suggested to Daily Mail Sport that a move for Rashford could be explored as early as January, with a desire to go back abroad.

A managerial change always puts things into flux and not least given that Pochettino said in 2022 that he'd 'always liked' Rashford, before adding: 'I think he's a great player. He just needs the confidence and for himself to believe, to put him at the top level. The quality is there for him.'

Pochettino is unlikely to have changed an opinion as solid as that one in the years that followed and so it will be curious to see if Rashford could become the athletic, pressing No9 in Benjamin Sesko's absence.

Rashford wants to feel the love and has shown what he can do when his confidence is high. It isn't right now but don't bet against Pochettino showing him that love.

Rashford has been linked with another move away but could become a pressing No 9

One of the more interesting profiles for Pochettino to consider.

On the face of it, Zirkzee lacks the intensity in the press and the mobility that Pochettino demands of his forwards.

Yet, Zirkzee can drop in, allowing the No10 to run in behind, which Pochettino values in a striker.

In the long term, expect Zirkzee to depart. In the short term, Pochettino may see him as a very specific tool to exploit certain opponents.

Tenacious defensively after improving immeasurably out of possession under Amorim, that's a big plus for Amad in the eyes of Pochettino.

He's among the glut of hybrid 10-wingers that United seem to stockpile and, once Sesko returns, Amad will find himself locked in a battle with Shea Lacey and Bryan Mbeumo for regular starts.

Amad's energy should give him the edge from day one to be a natural fit for Pochettino's high press.

Pochettino loves working with young players and Lacey is ready-made for that inverted winger style that the Argentine prefers, so he should be licking his lips at the prospect of more opportunities.

Lacey has played both off the right and as a No10 in academy teams and that stands him in good stead to operate in central areas, as well as isolate his full back one v one, which too many in this squad are not confident to do.

Lacey should be studying the development of Dele Alli under Pochettino and hoping he can bring his game on similarly.

Shea Lacey is (right) is a hugely promising youngster who will love working with Pochettino

Like Cunha, Mbeumo looked a more natural fit in Amorim's two-10s system and there are similarities that could put him back in those positions under Pochettino.

He's played a lot as a No 9 and may need to deputise there for the time being but the long-term dilemma for Pochettino will be the battle between Mbeumo, Amad and Lacey cutting in from the right.

It's one of the few areas of the pitch where there will be decent competition for places.

Mbeumo will need to find a position and master it or he may be caught in between roles.

Injured until, most likely, the end of January and so it will take some time for Pochettino to get his teeth into Sesko's development.

The Slovenian feels very close to Pochettino's ideal No9 profile given his athleticism, physicality in the air, ability to press from the front and his instinctive finishing ability.

Benjamin Sesko could raise his level under a manager who routinely improves forwards

Academy sources feel the teenager, who arrived for an initial £4million, has been unfairly criticised so far as he tries to adapt to a new club since moving up from Tottenham.

Thompson has picked up in recent academy games but in terms of his profile he looks more comfortable as a touchline winger, minus the blistering pace we usually see in that position.

His best bet is to remain in the academy and look towards a season-long loan next season.

One of the most intriguing academy prospects now that JJ Gabriel is closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

Ajayi looks physically capable of holding his own in first-team sessions and before a ball was kicked this term the development plan was to have him make a first-team debut before the season was out.

On-pitch failings may kick that can down the road but Ajayi is comfortable anywhere across the front line, has an acceleration that's invaluable and a technical level beyond his years.

Pochettino needs to take him under his wing to see what he can squeeze out of him before next summer.

VERDICT: Integrate into first-team training

#1889. AFCON 2027: The nine countries already qualified for the tournament

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 12:59

The first qualified teams for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. The tournament is scheduled for 19 June to 17 July 2027 in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

With four of the six qualifying matchdays played, nine of the 24 qualified nations for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. Here are all the countries that have qualified.

After the three host nations, who qualify automatically although they are taking part in the qualifiers, the fourth matchday of the 2027 qualifying campaign revealed six new qualified teams on 17 November 2026.

The co-host of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations is having a very mixed qualifying campaign. Benni McCarthy’s side did snatch a good point in South Africa (2-2), but they have only two points after four matchdays and had a scare at home against modest Eritrea (1-1).

Of the three host nations, Uganda are undoubtedly the ones having the best qualifying campaign, and the only ones to have won a match, a 1-0 victory over Libya. They are unbeaten after four matchdays and top their group ahead of Libya, Botswana and Tunisia.

The last of these automatically qualified nations, Tanzania have not necessarily made a strong impression. They have only two points after four matchdays, but they have just held Nigeria to a 0-0 draw, their best performance of the campaign so far.

One by one, the spots are being claimed! Here's who's qualified for #TotalEnergiesAFCON2027 after Matchday 4. ? https://t.co/uUJmkEBOVX

While waiting for the Court of Arbitration for Sport to rule on their status as 2025 champions or finalists, Senegal became the first team to secure their place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations on the pitch. After a laboured start in Mozambique (1-1), Patrick Vieira’s side strung together three wins, over Ethiopia and then Sudan twice, to confirm their ticket 24 hours after their matchday four game, thanks to a favourable result for Mozambique.

Held by Benin (1-1) in their opening game, Burkina Faso, round of 16 finalists in the last two editions, then dropped no more points, beating Central African Republic and then Mauritania twice. Amir Abdou’s side needed only four matchdays to qualify.

Round of 16 finalists in 2025, Benin will be present again for the Pamoja edition. After taking a good point from their trip to Burkina Faso (1-1), Gernot Rohr’s side dictated terms to Mauritania and then Central African Republic twice to secure qualification in November 2026, following Burkina Faso’s win over Mauritania.

After reaching the quarter-finals of the previous edition, Cameroon are taking these qualifiers very seriously. Held only in Congo, David Pagou’s side beat Comoros and Namibia twice to qualify after four matchdays, following Congo’s 1-0 defeat to Comoros.

Keen to go further than the quarter-finals, the ceiling reached in the last two editions, Mali confirmed their ambitions by being the only team along with Morocco to maintain a perfect record after four matchdays. World Cup-bound Cape Verde, Liberia and Rwanda twice all fell to Anthony Da Silva’s side, who qualified thanks to these wins.

As formidable as ever in these qualifiers, Morocco have a perfect 4/4 record, having beaten Gabon, Lesotho and then Niger twice. It was the second win over Niger, 1-0, thanks to a record-breaking goal from Abdellah Ouazane, that allowed Mohamed Ouahbi’s side to qualify.

#1888. Mauricio Pochettino has already introduced a Tottenham tradition at Manchester United

Mauricio Pochettino is having to squeeze a lot into his first days as Manchester United, but there will be time for one tried-and-tested tradition.

The Argentine touched down in Manchester on Wednesday, just hours after overseeing USA’s 2-0 win over Haiti in Cincinnati. The new head coach has conducted his first interview with club media, posed for photos and met the players.

On Thursday, Pochettino will take charge of his first training session at the club’s Carrington base before conducting his first press conference on Friday ahead of his first game on Sunday, which is a daunting trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool.

But there will see be time for a team dinner.

The Independent report that Pochettino plans on taking the players and staff out for a team bonding evening, and he will be picking up the tab.

It is a tradition Pochettino is said to have first introduced the custom during his time at Southampton, believing it was an important way to build relationships and strengthen the bond within a squad. He then did it at Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea.

It has previously been reported elsewhere that Pochettino held team dinners a number of times during his five-and-a-half-year tenure at Spurs.

With Pochettino taking charge midway through the campaign, there is no opportunity for a traditional pre-season or an extended period to get to know his players. The dinner will therefore provide an early chance for the 54-year-old and his coaching staff to assess the group's dynamics away from the training pitch.

Pochettino believes creating a strong sense of togetherness is essential to success, and the gathering will allow him to begin establishing his approach at Old Trafford. It will also give players and staff an opportunity to get to know their new manager and his backroom team in a more relaxed setting.

With a demanding schedule ahead, Pochettino will hope the occasion helps lay the foundations for a successful union between players and staff.

#1887. Bayern Munich vs FC Koln - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 18 Nov 2026 13:05

Bayern Munich can take a lead in the race for the Bundesliga title on Friday, when they welcome FC Koln to Allianz Arena.

The hosts are level on 21 points with second-placed Borussia Dortmund, who play on Saturday, whereas Koln are 15th with nine points after nine matchweeks.

Prior to the start of the November international break, Bayern emerged as 2-1 victors against Mainz 05, though they were wasteful in the final third, missing three of their four big chances while scoring just two of their 26 shots.

That win was their fourth in five games in all competitions, but it will be a concern that the team have only kept one clean sheet in their last eight matches.

The Bavarians have conceded 17 goals in their 16 fixtures this season, whereas they only conceded 13 times in the corresponding period in 2025-26.

Fans will hope the expected return of Vincent Kompany, who has not been in the dugout for his side's last five fixtures since collapsing on October 23, will help boost the team's performances at the back.

Bayern have drawn two of their three most recent contests at Allianz Arena, though they are yet to experience defeat at home, winning five of their seven clashes when playing as hosts.

Kompany's side have averaged five goals per game at home in the Bundesliga, while they only conceded four goals in their four league outings at Allianz Arena.

Koln were beaten 2-1 by Bayer Leverkusen on November 8 before the start of the international break, and it will concern supporters that the club have now won just one of their past eight top-flight games (W1, D4, L3).

Manager Rene Wagner will want his team to improve considerably in the final third given they have netted just twice in their last four league fixtures, blanking on two occasions.

A defeat on Friday would leave the visitors as low as 17th should Union Berlin and Schalke 04 claim three points in matchday 10, though it should be noted that only three points separate them from eighth-placed Stuttgart.

The Billy Goats' record against Bayern is predictably poor, with Wagner's side last beating their hosts in February 2011, and another loss would be their 22nd defeat in 24 meetings.

Koln's solitary victory in their five away matches this campaign came in the DFB-Pokal against Wurzburger Kickers in August, and they have since lost three games and settled for a stalemate once.

Bayern's injuries are still extensive despite the break from football, with left-back Alphonso Davies (hamstring) and goalkeeper Manuel Neuer (foot), as well as attackers Luis Diaz (hamstring) and Serge Gnabry (hamstring), among those to miss out.

Jonas Urbig will feature between the posts, while Josip Stanisic is almost certain to be stationed at left-back, with Dayot Upamecano and Jonathan Tah set to start as centre-backs.

In the forward line, Ballon d'or-winner Harry Kane may play ahead of a supporting cast consisting of Lennart Karl, Michael Olise and Nathaniel Brown.

Koln are also dealing with several injury issues, especially in defence considering both Timo Hubers and Rav van den Berg will be absent.

Joel Schmied, Jahmai Simpson-Pusey and Tom Krauss are the likely trio to start in the visitors' back three, while the club's attacking efforts will be led by forwards Marius Bulter and Said El Mala.

Urbig; Laimer, Upamecano, Tah, Stanisic; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Karl, Olise, Brown; Kane

Schwabe; Schmied, Simpson-Pusey, Krauss; Sebulonsen, Maina, Okon-Engstler, Johannesson, Sosa; Bulter, El Mala

Bayern Munich have shown that they are far from flawless at the back in recent months, so there should be openings for Koln.

However, the Bavarians have continued to be irresistible in attack despite their injuries, and they should be able to get the better of the visitors.

#1882. Mauricio Pochettino drops big tactics hint in first interview as Manchester United manager

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Mauricio Pochettino says he wants the Manchester United squad to feel "free" when playing in the new manager's first hint at his tactical approach.

Pochettino arrived at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday and on Thursday took charge of his first training session. On Sunday comes his first game, away at Anfield against Liverpool.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will be tasked with dragging Man Utd out of the relegation zone and back into the top echelons of English football.

The now-sacked Michael Carrick oversaw the club's worst start to a season in 40 years, and much of the malaise was put down to his tactical setups and a lack of energy from the players on the pitch.

And Pochettino, who is known for his hard drills in training, wants to bring the energy back to his players.

“It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,” Pochettino told the club's official website.

“Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

“The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

We need to love the players that we have, we need to support the players

“That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

“I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

On the significance of culture to success, he adds: “To create the culture is the most important [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

“We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.”

#1880. Mauricio Pochettino sends message to Manchester United fans in first interview as manager

Mauricio Pochettino has issued a message to Manchester United fans in his first interview as manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has replaced the sacked Michael Carrick, and flew in from the United States on Wednesday morning to begin his two-and-a-half-year contract.

Pochettino on Thursday oversaw his first training session as head coach, and has a quick turnaround before his first game in charge - which comes on Sunday at Anfield to face Liverpool.

The Argentine is aware he faces a baptism of fire at the home of a rival this weekend, and hopes to earn his connection with the fans by playing with "fight" and "for the win".

The fans need to see that we are going to fight ... and we are going to play for the win

"I don't want to ask nothing because I think always we demand, demand, demand to the fans, but we need to provide to the fans before we demand," he told the club's official website.

"I think we need to be the next to connect. We need to be the part that we create that energy that connect to the fans, to provide the fans.

"The fans need to see that we are going to fight, that we are Manchester United and we respect our history and we are going to play for the win. And for sure then our fans will be supporting us because what I hear and what I saw in the past, the supporters are amazing."

He continued: “I know very well what that game means and how important it is. The history talks for us and to what we need to expect.

“We need to make sure that we are brave and we are protagonists and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.”

#1879. Carlo Ancelotti and Raphinha see red: Security separate furious Brazil stars from officials after shock 3-2 defeat by Japan - with manager and captain sent off in bad-tempered friendly

Published: 11:31 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 12:52 EST, 14 November 2026

Carlo Ancelotti hit out at an 'inexperienced' referee after the Brazil boss and captain Raphinha were sent off in the closing stages of their shock 3-2 defeat by Japan.

Security staff were required to enter the pitch at full time to separate players from the officials, with Brazil having been left furious over the nature of Japan's stoppage time winner.

Ancelotti and Raphinha, who had been substituted, were among those to furiously protest following Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's late strike.

Singaporean referee Jansen Foo Chuan Hui had allowed play to continue after Takumi Minamino had made multiple challenges on Brazil midfielder Joao Gomes, before eventually coming away with the ball.

Amid Brazilian appeals for a foul, Japan launched a late attack with Sakamoto ultimately lifting the ball over goalkeeper Pedro Morisco.

Brazilian protests continued despite Japan's winner being confirmed by VAR, with Ancelotti and Raphinha being shown red cards by the referee for their reactions.

Security staff intervened after Brazil stars confronted the referee after their 3-2 defeat by Japan

Carlo Ancelotti was sent off as Brazil were beaten in stoppage time in their friendly in Singapore

Ancelotti criticised the 'inexperienced' referee following the match and revealed he had been told he had been sent off for failing to control his bench

🚨🚨| Raphinha and Carlo Ancelotti have been SENT OFF for Protesting. 🟥😳 pic.twitter.com/YoXrZW9N0U

'He gave me the red card because he said I was not able to control the bench, and that all the players were on the field, that is the reason,' Ancelotti said.

Ancelotti added: 'A pity the result, because we don't like to lose the game, but we have to look at what we did well. There are many things. Some players who played for the first time, who showed good quality. For 70 minutes, the team was good.

'The result, obviously, is conditioned by the attitude of the referee, who did not blow the whistle.

'But it's not his fault; it was a high-level match, and I think he didn't have the experience to manage this type of match.'

Barcelona star Raphinha claimed post-match that Brazil had also been angered over a potential handball in the build-up to Japan's opening goal, as well as seeing a penalty appeal waved away.

'First of all, I'd like to take this opportunity to apologise for my behaviour and for being sent off,' Raphinha told Globo.

'Sometimes it's hard to keep calm, especially after what I felt were so many refereeing errors during the match. I tried to speak to him several times, and not once did I feel he was open to discussion. I believe that he made many errors throughout the game, and that is unacceptable.

'In my view, their first goal involved a foul where the opponent took the ball off me with his hand. I think it's a foul, but I can understand why it wasn't given based on the current law.

Brazil captain Raphinha was also dismissed amid their protests over Japan's winning goal

Brazil had been convinced there had been a foul in the build-up to Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's winner

'Then there was the penalty in the first half, in my opinion it was a penalty, but he said no. Then, for their third goal, there was a clear foul on Joao Gomes. With the help of VAR, he eventually allowed the goal. It's very difficult not to talk about the refereeing.'

Brazil had fallen 2-0 down in the friendly with Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura scoring in the opening 20 minutes at Singapore's National Stadium.

Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr scored twice to level the match before Sakamoto's controversial late winner.

It is the second time Japan have beaten Brazil 3-2 in the past 18 months, but the five-time world champions did win 2-1 in their last-32 meeting at this summer's World Cup.

#1878. Man United transfer news: Five USA players who could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Old Trafford including teenage star

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 13:51, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 13:54

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has suggested that he could potentially target USA players in the upcoming transfer windows.

Pochettino has left his role with the United States to take charge of Man United, with the Argentine now in England preparing for Sunday's Premier League clash with Liverpool.

There has been a host of speculation in recent days surrounding potential USA arrivals at Man United, and here Sports Mole looks at five possible recruits for the 20-time English champions from the Stars and Stripes.

Man United need a striker due to Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems, and Balogun is currently being linked with a potential switch to Old Trafford.

The 25-year-old has scored 32 goals and registered 13 assists in 98 appearances for Monaco, while he has a record of 13 goals in 33 caps for USA.

Balogun's career started at Arsenal, but he only managed two goals in 10 appearances for the London club's first team before leaving in search of pastures new.

The United States international has since developed into an impressive forward, and a move to Man United during the January transfer window is thought to be possible.

Man United will overhaul their defence in 2027, and Freeman is believed to be very much on the club's radar, with that link growing since it was confirmed that Pochettino would be arriving.

Freeman, 22, made the move to Villarreal from Orlando City in January 2026, and he has scored once in 25 appearances for the Yellow Submarine.

The right-back has now been capped on 28 occasions by the USA, and there is a belief that he could secure a move to a major club in the not too distant future.

Man United are expected to sign at least two new full-backs next year, and one of those could potentially be Freeman, who has hugely impressed since his arrival in Spain.

Man United were linked with Adams long before Pochettino arrived, with the club thought to have considered moving for the USA international during the recent transfer window.

The 27-year-old has been capped on 64 occasions by his country and has featured on 77 occasions for Bournemouth, scoring three goals and registering seven assists.

Adams has actually now made 90 career appearances in the Premier League, including his time at Leeds United, and his high-energy style has attracted a host of attention.

The midfielder's contract at Bournemouth is due to expire in June 2028, and if a new deal is not agreed by next summer, there is expected to again be a lot of focus on his future.

McKennie has recently commented on claims that Man United could target USA players, and the 28-year-old is one of those to be linked with a move to Old Trafford.

The midfielder has experience of the Premier League, playing 19 times in the competition while on loan at Leeds United during the 2022-23 campaign.

McKennie has scored once and registered one assist in 11 appearances for Juventus this season, while he has played 73 times for his country.

The midfielder has made 241 appearances for Juventus, scoring 28 goals and registering 28 assists, and it would not be a shock to see him make the move to Old Trafford.

Hall has made a flying start to his senior career with the USA, scoring five times in six appearances, while the 18-year-old has 20 goals and six assists in 79 appearances for New York Red Bulls.

The teenager was on the scoresheet in both matches against Haiti ahead of Pochettino's exit, and a number of major clubs are believed to be keeping a close eye on his situation.

Should Hall continue to find the back of the net at an impressive rate, then a dream move to Man United could potentially be on the cards in the not too distant future.

#1877. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV

"Since the new manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

Smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

The noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

Bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

Murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

The current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

Safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

Newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

The pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

Jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls new signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

It looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

Newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

Wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

Just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

Newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

Three @premierleague games ✅Two @premierleague goals ✅ pic.twitter.com/B46guzqUjm

A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Two goals in two minutes leaves it intriguingly poisedIt's Newcastle 1-2 Bournemouth at half-time pic.twitter.com/iqTsAKRuVF

There will be three minutes of added time to finish off this breathless first half. Can Newcastle find a late leveller before the break or will Bournemouth restore their two-goal advantage?

It’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

What a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0

St James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

Newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Bournemouth’s high press works again and the ball breaks loose to Kluivert. He shoots from range and his deflected strike flies narrowly wide of the post.

Elanga’s frustrating afternoon continues as he collides with Silva as both players compete for the ball. The Newcastle winger picks up the game’s first yellow card because of the challenge.

The away side storm forward on the counter as Scott finds Truffert with a piercing pass. The Bournemouth left-back exploits the space vacated by Dedic. Truffert picks out Tavernier with a low cross, but the Englishman’s tame effort is saved by Hornicek. You would expect a lot more from Tavernier there, but Bournemouth look so dangerous going forward.

Bournemouth defend a couple of Newcastle corners in quick succession. The hosts are yet to create a notable chance.

There’s a real intensity to this game. Bournemouth are attempting to match Newcastle’s pace and physicality in every department. Just now, there was a really interesting battle between Willock and Adams, with the Newcastle man eventually winning a free-kick after a strong dribble.

Bournemouth look to have found a rhythm, with Scott dictating proceedings from the centre of the pitch. Truffert has done well early on to deal with Elanga’s attacking threat.

Bournemouth have taken the lead and Newcastle United supporters and [players are furious. Referee Rob Jones appeared to miss a pretty blatant shirt tug from Adrien Truffert stopping Anthony Elanga from spinning away, but that does not excuse the weak defending that led to the visitors scoring moments later.

Lewis Hall was beaten too easily by Rayan whose cross was only half cleared by Malick Thiaw but Amad Dedic got caught ball watching allowing Marcus Tavernier to steal in at the far post to bundle in a deflected shot from Evanilson.

Bournemouth should be two in front. A terrible pass from Sven Botman gifted the Brazilian the ball on the edge of the Newcastle box but he failed to hit the target.

Newcastle are rattled. They have not got to grips with Bournemouth in midfield and they are crowding out Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock whenever Matthias Jaissle’s side look to go direct.

We wondered how Newcastle would match up against Bournemouth and they have looked second best so far.

What a chance for Bournemouth to double their lead! What is Botman doing? The centre-back misplaces a pass and Evanilson latches onto the mistake. The striker runs in on goal, but blazes the glaring opportunity over the bar. That’s a huge let-off for Newcastle. Evanilson must do better from that range.

Scott’s deflected strike richochets into Tavernier’s path, with the Bournemouth attacker sneaking in behind Dedic, who switches off. Tavernier then directs a half-volley into the roof of the net. Newcastle are furious. They feel they should of been awarded a free-kick after a earlier tussle between Truffert and Elanga. Both players are pulling each other’s shirts. After a quick VAR check, the goal stands and the away fans are delighted.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Dedic shows his quality by intercepting a pass from deep, skipping away from Scott’s sliding challenge and then dribbling all the way to the byline. He can’t quite win a corner, but his efforts are appreciated by the Newcastle faithful.

Newcastle attempt to counter through Wissa and Willock, with the latter passing to Barnes. However, the former Leicester man cuts inside and runs into trouble, causing the opening to disappear.

Tavernier takes it and fires a low effort around the wall, but Hornicek is there to get down low and make a relatively routine save.

Elanga has made a busy start to this game. The winger’s pace is so explosive. Bournemouth then win a free-kick on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area as Miley catches Kluivert. Mulitple Bournemouth players are standing over this.

The visitors get us under way at St James’ Park. Which German manager will prevail?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the new season but have people got a little carried away?

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1876. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-final?

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents was revealed on Tuesday night as Norway produced a stunning comeback from 2-0 down pip Denmark to the runners-up spot behind Portugal in Group A4 by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1875. Man Utd transfer news: Red Devils join Man City in 'race' for Bayern Munich sensation

By Saikat Mandal | 18 Nov 2026 14:28

Manchester United and Manchester City are reportedly showing keen interest in signing Bayern Munich sensation Leonard Prescott.

The 17-year-old is a highly-rated young goalkeeper who has progressed through Bayern's youth ranks, but several clubs are now monitoring his situation.

Arsenal have reportedly been tracking the youngster, while contract talks with Bayern have not progressed as hoped.

Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Italian giants Juventus have also made contact over a potential move for Prescott, whose current contract is due to expire next summer.

According to TeamTalk, Manchester United and Manchester City have also joined the race for his signature and made contact with Prescott's representatives.

There are suggestions that the teenager could potentially develop into the best goalkeeper in Europe in his age group.

A move away from Bayern is now a genuine possibility, although the German champions could still convince the highly-rated youngster to commit his long-term future to the Allianz Arena.

Prescott does not turn 18 until September, meaning he would be unable to move to England before 2028.

There is a growing feeling that the current season could be Manuel Neuer's last at the club.

Jonas Urbig has proved to be an able deputy, and the German goalkeeper is expected to take over as Bayern's first choice once Neuer hangs up his gloves.

Prescott therefore faces an uphill battle to establish himself, with Bayern reportedly considering the signing of another goalkeeper to serve as their number two next summer.

Bayern rate the teenager highly, but his representatives are not entirely convinced by the pathway being laid out for him at the Allianz Arena, offering encouragement to the interested Premier League clubs.

#1874. Nations League quarter-final draw simulated: England get favourable tie as Spain handed France rematch

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

There was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

So ahead of Friday's draw, who will be paired with who? Well, the four seeded sides each have three possibilities as teams from the same group cannot be paired with each other.

As a result, a knockout stage simulator has determined their potential opponents in the quarter-final and it's safe to say the results are quite fascinating.

In this simulation, England have been paired with the Netherlands in what would be a repeat of the semi-final during the inaugural season of the Nations League.

#1872. Majority of clubs vote for extra legal protection for Premier League chiefs

Premier League board members have been given extra legal protection amid the threat of actions linked to the Manchester City case.

Eighteen clubs are reported to have supported changes to the league’s articles at a clubs meeting in central London on Thursday, which extend protections provided to individual board members to enable them to freely carry out their duties.

A 14-club majority is required for votes to be carried, and it was understood to have been comfortably above that.

The change comes after City sponsor Etihad said in September it was considering legal action over the “damaging” implications of the independent commission’s guilty verdict against the club.

The airline was not named in the verdict, which found City had benefited from “sham” arrangements to inflate revenue and disguise costs to avoid breaching Premier League and UEFA rules. City have appealed against the verdict. Another City sponsor, Etisalat, was reported by The Times to be considering similar action earlier this week.

The Press Association understands the issue was brought to a vote in order to bring the league’s individual legal cover in line with similar companies – including many of its clubs – and that these articles had not been looked at since the league’s inception in 1992.

There was no indication of any cap on the costs clubs could be exposed to as a result of the change to the league’s articles, and no wider discussion or questions raised on the City case despite this being the first shareholders’ meeting since the verdict was published on September 29.

Club executives also received a first update of the season from referees’ chief Howard Webb.

He is understood to have accepted the 10th round of matches immediately before the November international break had been especially difficult.

Six on-field errors were identified by the Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel which were not corrected by VAR intervention.

This is in part due to the high bar for intervention being operated this season, where referee’s on-field calls can only be overturned where it is felt the error was not a clear and obvious one.

#1871. Real Madrid star Arda Guler rewarded for what is set to be his best campaign yet

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 15:06, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 15:07

Real Madrid have announced that Arda Guler has signed a new contract at Bernabeu until the end of the 2031-32 campaign.

The Turkey international made the move to Bernabeu from Fenerbahce in the summer of 2023, and he has represented the capital giants on 126 occasions, scoring 22 goals and registering 32 assists in the process.

Guler has started the campaign with four goals and seven assists in 14 appearances in all competitions, including three goals and five assists in 12 La Liga outings.

Real Madrid have announced that the 21-year-old has agreed a new deal in the Spanish capital until the summer of 2032.

"Real Madrid C. F. and Arda Guler have agreed to extend the contract of our player, who will remain linked to the club until June 30, 2032," read a statement from the capital giants.

Guler has started 10 of Real Madrid's 12 La Liga matches this season, demonstrating his importance for Los Blancos, although he has only played in two of their four Champions League league stage fixtures this term.

The playmaker missed the team's 2026-27 European opener against Inter Milan through suspension, while he was rested against AEK Athens in their last game in the competition.

Guler has not scored more than six times in a campaign for Real Madrid since his arrival, but he is already just two goals off that total in November.

Real Madrid won La Liga and the Champions League during Guler's first campaign at the club, but he only featured on 12 occasions in 2023-24.

Guler has won five trophies during his time at Bernabeu, but this could be his best campaign yet both from a personal and team point of view.

Guler is expected to be in the starting team when Real Madrid continue their La Liga campaign against Celta Vigo on November 21.

The playmaker will then be hoping to make his third Champions League appearance of the season when Los Blancos face PSV Eindhoven in the competition on November 24.
