#1869. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1

Pierre Sage has his first win while Alvaro Arbeloa has lost his first three Premier League games and go to Anfield next Saturday. Frank de Boer vibes.

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

Brighton 1 Leeds 1. Pascal Gross missed a late sitter and Leeds are still winless in Brighton’s ‘new’ stadium in 11 visits.

It remains 0-0 so Spurs are goalless in three, both sides remain winless.

Iliman Ndiaye took a knock and has come off after treatment. He has sat on the bench, though, rather than headed down the tunnel, which suggests it is not an injury.

Enzo Le Fee equalises from the penalty spot.

VAR does not intervene after Lewis-Potter was penalised for holding. Le Fee chipped a pen straight at the keeper there last season.

Ellis Simms with the latest, clocking Donnarumma flush in the face with his close-range effort.

And it’s a third goal from a  left-back, but this time it’s the substitute Ben Chilwell.

Jaidon Anthony bundled the ball in but had used his hands.

And Mykhailo Mudryk is on for his first appearance since November 2024.

Forest are feeling aggrieved over that disallowed goal. Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot.

Big cheer for Phil Foden when he came on for Rayan Cherki. Cherki has been creative for City and this might be trying another mode of attack for Enzo Maresca or saving legs for the Champions League in midweek. They have two full days of rest before facing Porto on Tuesday.

That is a big chance for Coventry. Loum Tchaouna got room in the penalty area and it needed Gianluigi Donnarumma to save low to his right.

Luka Vuskovic heads in from an inswinging corner.

Controversy at the City Ground – and it’s again a result of Var.

Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Neco Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goalline.

The goal did go to Var for a possible handball by Williams, and it was ruled that the Wales international did handle it. Did look very harsh.

Coventry are still in this game but City have their chances to put them away. Enzo was deemed offside when he set up a strike for Haaland. The UK’s most expensive player has got better during this game.

Looks like it will be ruled out for handball.

Vitaly Janelt breaks the deadlock after Brentford were battered in the first half.

Keith Andrews is a brave manager. Having been forced into a change after 17 minutes when his captain, Nathan Collisn was injured, he shook it up at half-time by replacing three of his biggest signings, Kayode, Sangaré and Ouattara for Hickey, Yarmoliuk and Anthony.

There is also the option of Dominic Solanke on the bench too.

Because of the 4½ minute VAR check for the Ballard ‘goal’ and an injury to Nathan Collins that forced the Bees’ captain off.

Forest are embarking on a new era under Oliver Glasner with a style of play that will take time to implement.

The best chance fell to one of Tottenham’s new arrivals, Omar Marmoush, but he drilled a shot wide of the post.

The big headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

#1868. Antonio Rudiger compares Kylian Mbappe to Cristiano Ronaldo in Real Madrid defence

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 15:20

Real Madrid defender Antonio Rudiger has launched a passionate defence of Kylian Mbappe's contribution to the team, drawing a striking comparison with Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and Gareth Bale to challenge criticism of the Frenchman's defensive work.

Mbappe has been one of Madrid's most prolific players since arriving from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024, reaching 100 goals for the Spanish giants despite their struggles to win major silverware over the past two seasons.

However, his extraordinary goalscoring record has not prevented questions being raised about his willingness to press opponents and contribute when Madrid are out of possession.

The issue has become particularly prominent under Jose Mourinho, whose demanding approach requires his players to maintain their defensive organisation.

Rudiger believes some of those expectations are misplaced, arguing that a forward of Mbappe's quality should be judged primarily on his ability to decide matches.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with The Athletic, the former Chelsea centre-back questioned whether it made sense to demand the same defensive responsibilities from a player who has already delivered 100 goals for Madrid.

"Should I tell Mbappe [...] to do my job? It makes no sense," Rudiger said.

The German then pointed to one of the most successful attacking partnerships in Real Madrid's history to explain his position.

Rudiger believes Madrid's previous success offers an important lesson about how to accommodate outstanding attacking players.

He recalled the celebrated partnership of Ronaldo, Bale and Benzema, who spearheaded the club's attack during a period that produced four Champions League titles between 2014 and 2018.

The trio were renowned for their individual attacking qualities and ability to deliver decisive moments in major matches.

Rudiger suggested that Madrid did not achieve those successes by constantly scrutinising their forwards' defensive contributions.

He pointed to the achievements of the three players before insisting that discussion of attackers should not always revolve around their work without the ball.

His argument is particularly relevant to Mbappe, whose goals have frequently provided Madrid with a decisive advantage even when the team's collective performances have attracted criticism.

The French international has continued to deliver exceptional numbers in front of goal, although Madrid have struggled to translate his individual productivity into the trophies expected at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Rudiger's comments do not suggest that Mbappe should be exempt from defensive responsibilities. Rather, the defender believes the rest of the team must find an effective balance around players whose greatest value comes in attacking positions.

The comparison with Ronaldo is especially significant given the Portuguese forward's standing at Madrid, where he scored 450 goals in 438 appearances and helped establish an era of sustained European dominance.

Mbappe has already been compared to Ronaldo following his spectacular individual performances for Madrid, but Rudiger has approached the comparison from a different perspective.

For the experienced defender, the question is how Madrid can create the conditions for their most influential attackers to flourish.

Rudiger also addressed another recurring criticism of Madrid's squad: the difficulty of managing a dressing room filled with established international stars.

The 33-year-old acknowledged that the club's collection of strong personalities can create challenges for any manager.

He referred to Rafael Benitez and Julen Lopetegui, whose spells in charge of Madrid ended prematurely, as examples of coaches who encountered similar difficulties.

"It's not a myth. That's the reality," Rudiger admitted when discussing the influence of big personalities at the club.

His comments offer an insight into the environment Mourinho has inherited since returning to Madrid during the summer.

The Portuguese manager has been tasked with restoring the club's success after two seasons without a major trophy, with Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior among the players expected to lead that recovery.

Rudiger spoke positively about Mourinho's influence, revealing that the manager had contacted him towards the end of last season to explain his plans and express his desire to keep the German at the club.

He also described a lighter side to Mourinho's personality, explaining that the former Manchester United and Chelsea boss enjoys telling jokes in the dressing room while maintaining a far more demanding approach on the training pitch.

The defender extended his support to Vinicius, who has experienced a difficult start to the season and faced increased competition for his position.

Rudiger insisted that the Brazilian continues to work hard to improve his performances and remains an important figure in Madrid's plans.

Vinicius has recently rediscovered his goalscoring form with Brazil, scoring five times across two international friendlies against Japan and Singapore.

His return presents Mourinho with another selection decision as Madrid prepare to resume their domestic campaign.

For Rudiger, however, the responsibility for restoring Madrid's success cannot rest solely on the willingness of Mbappe, Vinicius or Bellingham to defend.

His comparison with Ronaldo's celebrated attacking partnership reflects a broader conviction that Madrid must find a collective structure capable of making the most of their attacking talent.

#1867. CM: Milan could compete with Newcastle and Aston Villa for Lille gem Ngoy

There’s no shortage of defenders being linked to AC Milan currently and a new name has been proposed to the club today.

With a desire to add more cover in the defence, Milan are keeping a keen eye on the mercato and several profiles are arising that could be of interest. Of course, there are a few headliners, but there are also some rising talents that could explode at San Siro.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Calciomercato.com write that the Rossoneri are beginning to take an interest in Nathan Ngoy, the Belgian defender who is rapidly progressing. Like Diego Moreira, he also scored his first goal for the Red Devils against Italy and the future looks bright for him.

Said to be following in Vincent Kompany’s footsteps, he’s part of the rebuilding of the Belgian defence and has become a starter since the World Cup.

It’s also a reason why his value has risen so much in recent months; after the summer, he was believed to be worth €20 and €25 million, but he’s now got a valuation of around €40m.

Goncalo Inacio and Virgil van Dijk are the main names for the defence currently. Yet, the links between the Diavolo and Lille could help make a route to Ngoy easier, as could his international teammates who play at San Siro.

Newcastle and Aston Villa are also keen on the young defender, so he’s certainly one to watch in the future and it could be a major coup for Milan.

#1866. Liverpool XI vs Manchester United: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Premier League

Andoni Iraola should have a relatively healthy squad to choose from when he selects Liverpool’s starting XI to face arch-rivals Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday.

The Reds are still waiting on the availability of club captain Virgil van Dijk and midfielder Ryan Gravenberch.

Both missed out on international duty with the Netherlands - van Dijk pulling out of the squad after concerns over a ‘little niggle’ he has been carrying.

Dominik Szoboszlai has struggled with fitness in recent weeks, but came through two games for Hungary unscathed. Iraola will have also have been pleased by the news that Alexander Isak was rested for Sweden’s second game of the international break, leaving the Reds’ top scorer in top condition for the weekend.

In goal, veteran Alisson will start in between the sticks. Van Dijk’s decision to drop out of the Netherlands squad seemed precautionary, and it is hoped he will feature here.

The Dutchman is building a strong connection with Jeremy Jacquet at the back. Milos Kerkez is first choice at left back, but injuries at right-back have caused Iraola headaches all season.

Ronald Araujo has deputised on the right for the majority of the season, and he will likely start there again.

A fully fit Szoboszlai is Liverpool’s best midfielder, so the Hungarian is slated to start alongside Alexis Mac Allister in the heart of the Reds’ team.

Florian Wirtz saw his best run of form since signing for the club last summer interrupted slightly by injury, but the German should soon get back into a rhythm with another start at number 10.

On the wings, Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo are emerging as first choices - but it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Victor Munoz start ahead of Barcola.

Up top, Isak will once again lead the line. The Swede will hope to add to his seven Premier League goals in nine top-flight appearances.

#1865. Mauricio Pochettino 'honoured' and 'privileged' to be at Man United as Red Devils reign officially begins

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 15:26, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 15:27

Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United's new head coach, with the Argentine arriving at the club's Carrington training complex.

The Argentine oversaw USA's 2-0 win over Haiti in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final, which kicked off at midnight on Tuesday UK time, before flying to Manchester to begin work with the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino's time as head coach of Man United has now officially started, with the club posting a video of the 54-year-old arriving on their X account.

"Very excited to be here. It's an honour. It's a privilege to be in this amazing club. Looking forward to starting work," said Pochettino.

He's here. Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino! ??? https://t.co/MOhRCv79hq

Man United appointed Pochettino as their new head coach at the end of last week, but the club agreed that he could finish his November commitments with the USA before arriving on Wednesday, as the Red Devils prepare for Sunday's Premier League game at Liverpool.

The 54-year-old's assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino travelled to Manchester earlier this week.

Pochettino is set to speak to the media at Carrington on Friday afternoon.

Players who have represented their countries during the international break will arrive at Carrington from Thursday, so it is a quick turnaround ahead of the Liverpool clash.

Pochettino will hardly have time to take stock after the Liverpool game, as Man United will then head to Portugal at the start of next week to prepare to take on Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

The Argentine led the USA to the last-16 stage of the 2026 World Cup and also reached the 2025 Gold Cup final during his time in charge.

In an exit statement on Instagram, Pochettino said: "I am proud of what we achieved. When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team.

"This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally.

"Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

"I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves."

Pochettino has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the Premier League, while he has left his USA role with a record of 23 wins, two draws and 12 defeats from his 37 matches at the helm.

#1863. So much pace and potential, not enough positive impact... surely Scotland must now redefine the role of Ben Gannon-Doak?

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 12:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:14 EST, 14 November 2026

In an age where much of the football on show in the English Premier League is so robotic as to be almost unwatchable, flashes of individual brilliance are increasingly becoming things to be cherished.

Across his time at Liverpool and Bournemouth, Ben Gannon-Doak has sporadically distinguished himself as someone who can light up a game by doing something out of the blue and out of the ordinary.

As many a defender will testify, that electric burst of pace across a short distance makes him unplayable at times. He has an X-factor which sets him apart from the crowd.

What a shame that injuries have restricted his number of appearances to this point. Since moving south from Celtic in 2022, including a loan spell with Middlesbrough, Gannon-Doak has played fewer than 50 times.

At the very time in his career when he could have done with smoothing off the rough edges, he’s spent far too long rehabilitating from one setback or another.

In the build-up to Friday’s match with North Macedonia, Sebastien Pocognoli spoke about how encouraged he was that the player was finally seeing more game time on the south coast, partly as a result of the team’s maiden voyage in Europe.

Ben Gannon-Doak started in a right wing-back role and had an energetic yet frustrating night

The hope of all concerned was that the recent run of matches which the winger had so evidently needed would translate into a more accomplished display in a Scotland jersey. Alas, this proved to be wishful thinking.

Even against very ordinary opposition, Gannon-Doak’s display proved to be another frustrating watch for the Tartan Army.

Time and time again, he brought them to the edge of their seats by facing up a white jersey and seemingly disappearing in a puff of smoke towards the line. Rarely, however, did the end product materialise.

For a winger with such blinding speed to continually struggle with the all-important final ball is a difficult thing to repeatedly witness.

We shall never know, of course, if the player’s crossing ability would be better by this stage if he hadn’t endured such wretched luck with injuries. But you suspect it’s now just about as good as it’s ever going to be.

The trouble for Pocognoli is that the quality of the delivery from wing-backs into the penalty box is arguably the most important facet of his preferred 3-4-3 system.

When it breaks down, as it did so often against the group outsiders, the whole thing threatens to grind to a halt.

Gannon-Doak's crossing remains an area of concern for Scotland given his wide position

On his record-equalling 102nd cap, Andy Robertson was also guilty of being wasteful on the other flank. Given we know what the skipper has delivered down the years, though, we can write that off as merely a bad night at the office.

The difference with Gannon-Doak is that we’ve rarely seen him tear it up on the flank in a Scotland jersey. So much pace and potential. Not enough positive outcomes when it comes to delivering crosses. In 21 matches, he has three assists and one goal. Those aren’t great numbers.

Just how long do you persevere with a player who doesn’t look to have the requisite skill set for such a specialised and vital position?

Aaron Hickey clearly doesn’t have the pace of the man who he replaced late on, yet he’s hardly a slouch. He is, though, more switched on defensively. And he does know how to cross a football.

It was telling that Gannon-Doak’s most positive contribution of the night against the group outsiders came when he left his station to move infield and take Oli McBurnie’s pass in his stride with the score standing at one-apiece.

His surge towards the goal initially looked like it had been hampered by a heavy touch only for VAR to correctly identify that he’d been impeded by the goalkeeper. He earned his corn in that moment.

John McGinn’s conversion from 12 yards, his second goal of the night, spared Pocognoli’s blushes after a display which didn’t exactly inspire.

That sequence of play certainly raised the possibility that Gannon-Doak could be utilised to better effect in another role.

Gannon-Doak's forward burst led to the award of a penalty and hinted at an alternative role

If played more centrally, his crossing – undoubtedly his weak spot – would not be such an issue. But the acceleration and driving runs would still be there to cause chaos in and around the penalty box. That will always be his strong suit.

To get the best out of him, maybe the manager needs to redefine him.

Any redeployment would, obviously, create another issue. If Pocognoli remains wedded to the current system, it seems likely that Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson will occupy the two holding berths.

Ahead of them, and behind the main striker, McGinn and Scott McTominay are virtually undroppable. It might be the case then, that Gannon-Doak is eventually utilised as an impact sub. Yet, it would not be a plan without its merits.

He’s got a part to play in this set-up. Probably just not where he’s currently being positioned.

You’d be surprised, frankly, if he started in St Gallen on Monday. Switzerland are a far superior side to North Macedonia, already assured of promotion to League A by topping the section and looking to end this campaign with a flourish against a Scotland side they beat comfortably at Hampden.

They’ll ask far more questions of Pocognoli’s side. It feels like a task more suited to Hickey.

Scotland, collectively, will need to buck up their ideas if they are to stand any chance of emerging with a positive outcome or, at the least, some credit.

Scotland fans are desperate to see Gannon-Doak succeed but a little change might be needed

There was a flatness to Friday’s performance, especially in a first half in which the much-vaunted high-press was conspicuous by its absence.

The passing was too safe and predictable. The tempo was low and the play was unimaginative. By half-time, the visitors had fashioned the better chance when Enis Bardhi smashed the ball into the side net.

Scotland were markedly better after the turnaround. After Billy Gilmour’s scarcely believable miss, they were deserving of the opener which came when McGinn burst into the box and lashed home after fine work from Che Adams.

Stemming straight from a corner, North Macedonia’s equaliser – which ended their eight-game goal drought – asked a serious question of Pocognoli’s players.

To their credit, they stepped up with Gannon-Doak’s foray into the box causing the moment of indecision on which the game swung.

The manner of a first Hampden win for Pocognoli won’t live long in the memory. The fervent hope is that it proves to be the start of something.

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 15:57, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 16:00

Former Manchester United captain Ashley Young has urged the Red Devils to sell captain Bruno Fernandes next year and bring in Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White as his replacement.

Fernandes' future with the Red Devils is currently the subject of much speculation, with the Portugal international's contract at Old Trafford due to expire next summer.

Man United do have the option to activate a further year to take the 32-year-old to the summer of 2028, but it is understood that Fernandes has rejected the chance to sign a fresh deal with the club.

The Portuguese had an outstanding 2025-26 Premier League season, scoring nine goals and registering 21 assists in 35 appearances, while he has six goals and three assists in 14 appearances for the Red Devils this term.

Fernandes has struggled to show his best form for much of the campaign, though, and a departure next year is seen as possible.

Young, who played for Man United between 2011 and 2020, has urged the 20-time English champions to make a move for Forest's Gibbs-White.

The 26-year-old has scored 37 goals and registered 38 assists in 180 matches for Forest in all competitions, including one goal and three assists in nine Premier League outings this term.

“Bruno has been fantastic for Manchester United. He has been, and no one can say that he hasn’t,” Young told Standard Sport.

“There's obviously been a few things that have come up of late. If a club like Manchester United are going to build a team around him, he's going to be 33 next year.

“If it was me, I would be looking at going to get another number 10 and build it around him. I'd go and get Morgan Gibbs-White. I think he's got 18 months left on his contract.

"He's established in the Premier League, he’s a leader, he's showing his qualities at Nottingham Forest. And I'm sure Nottingham Forest won't thank me for saying that.”

Gibbs-White has long been linked with a move away from Forest, but he signed a new deal with the club in the summer of 2025 after a proposed switch to Tottenham Hotspur failed to materialise.

The Englishman is surely in line for a move to an elite club in the not too distant future, and he would be an ideal signing for Man United given his skill set and Premier League experience.

Man United will be active in the summer of 2027, and if Fernandes moves on, then Gibbs-White could be the perfect replacement for the Portuguese.

#1858. Man United news: KMI Panel delivers surprise verdict over Aston Villa equaliser

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 16:00

The KMI Panel has unanimously claimed that Manchester United's decisive equaliser against Aston Villa was correctly awarded.

In the final Premier League match before the November international break, the Red Devils and Villans played out a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford.

Villa twice held two-goal advantages - at 2-0 and 4-2 - before United scored twice in added-on time to earn a deserved share of the spoils.

However, there were question marks over whether Patrick Dorgu's last-gasp equaliser should have stood.

United goalkeeper Senne Lammens, who had joined the attack for a corner, seemingly deliberately made contact with opposite number Zion Suzuki without making an attempt for the ball.

Despite it appearing clear that Lammens's only intention was to make contact with Suzuki, it has been deemed that the referee and VAR were correct not to award or advise a foul.

A five-person KMI Panel all determined that a foul had not been committed by Lammens, subsequently leading to VAR not being required to intervene.

The KMI Panel said: "Although Lammens turned away from the ball, the contact he made on Suzuki was not impactful."

Aston Villa chief Damian Vidagany took to social media in the day after the match to claim that all 20 Premier League clubs had been informed before the start of the season that such an action from any player would be penalised.

The incident was one which brought up a genuine debate over whether the goal should have stood, but the fact that the KMI Panel voted unanimously against a foul being committed could open a can of worms.

Managers and players will, logically, now attempt to replicate the level of interference from Lammens, aware that they could avoid punishment from officials.

#1857. Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session hit by concerning security breach

Manchester United have been left red-faced after a drone covertly filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session and posted the footage to YouTube.

The Argentine, who signed up to replace Michael Carrick as United’s head coach last week, arrived at Carrington on Wednesday to start work with his new club.

With United languishing in the drop zone, Pochettino faces a brutal opening fixture of his reign, away at Liverpool.

But his preparations for that match have already been compromised in a concerning security breach at United’s training centre, after a drone secretly recorded 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first session with the club, with footage posted on YouTube for all to see.

The drone does not appear to have entered Carrington’s airspace at any point, but footage filmed with a zoom lens shows the session in clear detail.

The YouTube channel which posted the clip followed it up with a statement claiming they had broken no laws by recording the session as the airspace around Carrington is unrestricted.

No players or staff caught in the footage appeared to be aware of the fact they were being filmed. At the time of writing, the clip has accrued over 40,000 views.

The footage shows the United squad working in two groups. One was being put through a rondo on one pitch, while Pochettino led the other through what appeared to be a tactical session on another. Both groups appeared to comprise a blend of first-team and academy players.

Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Standard Sport.

#1854. “We needed to make a move” – Moncada explains Milan’s multi-year pursuit of Cisse

Geoffrey Moncada, today, has given a bit of insight into how long AC Milan were trying to sign Alphadjo Cisse.

When Milan signed Cisse, there was a bit of a mixed reaction. Although he was seen as a talent for the future, the money could’ve been spent on a first-team acquisition, with the squad lacking in certain areas.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, though, everyone would be glad that the decision was made to sign the young Italian. To say he’s exploded this season would be an understatement and he’s perhaps the biggest gem at the club right now.

Speaking to Calcio e Pepe, as Francesco Nasato relayed on X, Moncada went through the process of the Rossoneri’s scouting of Cisse.

“We had a scout who worked near Verona and he immediately pointed out this boy to us, Alphadjo Cisse, who played for the Under-17s and then for the Primavera, and then for the Under-20s. So we went to see him and he was very interesting.

“Two or three years ago, we launched Milan Futuro. Our idea was to sign him for that team a year earlier, but we couldn’t reach an agreement with Hellas Verona. They wanted to keep him and decided to send him on loan to Serie B.

“We followed him very closely in Serie B, too, and he literally exploded there in the first six months. We told ourselves he’d made such a good transition from the Primavera and Verona’s bench to Serie B that we needed to make a move.

“It was winter and we had to hurry. If he had gone to PSV and you had wanted to buy him later, perhaps after playing in the Champions League, the price would have risen to €30 or €40 million. Sometimes you have to speed things up a bit.”

Considering the club had followed him since he was in the Under-17s, it’s a good thing they eventually managed to sign him, especially with the way he’s started at San Siro.

#1853. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the eight teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position was Group A4 was confirmed after their win over Wales on Tuesday, though it is Norway joining them in the knockout phases following a remarkable comeback win against Denmark.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

Pot 1: France, England, Germany, Portugal

Pot 2: Belgium, Spain, Netherlands, Norway

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

The first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The final tournament is scheduled for June 2027.

#1852. Man United must not pass up on incredible Alejandro Balde opportunity in January

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 16:56

Manchester United could reportedly sign Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde on loan during the January transfer window without having to pay his full wages.

Balde's future remains the subject of much speculation, with the Spain international expected to leave the Catalan outfit when the winter market opens for business.

Man United were linked with the left-back over the summer but were ultimately unable to progress due to the 23-year-old's desire to remain at Camp Nou.

It has been a frustrating campaign for Balde, who has been restricted to just five appearances for Barcelona, and he has not started a single game at club level this term.

The defender has allegedly accepted that he will need to leave Barcelona in January for the sake of his career, and Man United are desperate to bring in a left-back.

According to RAC, Barcelona are keen to move Balde on in January in order to free up space for them to sign a centre-back.

The report claims that the La Liga champions would prefer a permanent exit, but a loan deal is also possible, with Man United not even needing to cover his full wage packet.

A partial wage contribution could potentially be accepted by Barcelona providing that enough space in their budget is made to bring in a new player.

Balde has made 173 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions, scoring three goals and registering 21 assists in the process.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a frustrating campaign for Balde, but he has only just turned 23 and not too long ago was seen as one of the best full-backs in world football.

Luke Shaw's injury problems have caused a real issue for Man United at left-back this term, with Diogo Dalot finding it difficult in that area of the field.

Patrick Dorgu is now back to fitness, but the majority of his best work for the 20-time English champions has occurred in the final third of the field.

It is vital that the Red Devils address the major squad issue in the winter market, and it is important that the club do not pass up on an incredible opportunity to bring in Balde.

#1851. Mauricio Pochettino leaves behind a negligible legacy at USMNT... where raised standards never materialized into results as tearful Argentine bolts for Man United

Published: 13:29 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:42 EST, 14 November 2026

Perhaps it's incredibly cynical, and maybe too harsh, to call the tears that fell down the face of Mauricio Pochettino 'performative.' But it's the first word that came to mind – followed by 'surprising' and 'a bit much.'

It was only four months ago when the Argentine who had been atop the United States' men's national team since 2024 signed a contract extension to stay on board for another four years.

'We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field,' Pochettino said when his contract was signed.

Yet, after a few months and one international window, that experiment to make a 'lasting impact' has ended. Pochettino may have cried because he fell in love with the country, but it's not like he got fired. Instead, he's off to lead one of the world's greatest football brands in Manchester United.

So now the question turns to the legacy Pochettino leaves behind. Plenty of American soccer writers and fans point to the spirit the former Chelsea boss created and how he helped to energize a team which had been bogged down by past coaches.

But Pochettino's results don't scream success. The World Cup finish was nothing special compared to his peers, his record against the best nations the USA faced was poor and he'll leave as the first full-time USMNT manager in nearly 30 years to not win at least one trophy.

Mauricio Pochettino cried as he left the United States' top job for Manchester United

Pochettino's USMNT played exciting football, but ultimately didn't progress past the norm

But any potential for further growth evaporated when the Argentine returned to England

By all accounts, the greatest thing Pochettino did was install a hungry, all-in-or-nothing culture in a team bogged down by an earth-rocking scandal and a poor 2024 Copa America run.

But he did so in a way that often left the biggest players of the USMNT system behind. Rather than keep a consistent core of his best players around, he seemed intent on tinkering with the lineup in each window.

The results reflect that instability. Leading to the World Cup, Pochettino played 12 games against sides in the top 30 of the FIFA World Rankings. He won just three fixtures – drawing once and losing the remaining eight.

All the while, he was linked to returns to Europe. Pochettino may have said in his exit press conference that he 'never said I wanted to go back to the Premier League' but the Premier League certainly wanted him – especially Tottenham.

Come World Cup time, Pochettino's team finally seemed to gel with a scintillating style of play never before seen in the USMNT.

But it all crashed down after the Round of 32 game against Bosnia when Folarin Balogun's red card was (as this American will admit) deviously overturned. The noise and controversy led to the Americans' embarrassment at the hands of Belgium on home soil.

A summer of exciting soccer for the USMNT followed years of hard resets and mixed results

It all fell apart with a demolition by Belgium, leaving Pochettino without any success

The Yanks were not expected to go much further than the last 16. But branding Pochettino's time atop the USMNT a 'success' on the back of this World Cup performance is giving him too much credit – especially considering the four prior managers to take the US to the World Cup all made it to that stage of the tournament as well.

With his departure confirmed, Pochettino is the first USMNT manager to leave the post without any silverware since the 1998 departure of Steve Sampson, who hadn't been a professional manager before being appointed to the job.

Even though he achieved little in terms of results, players praised Pochettino's leadership and development skills, which shouldn't be ignored.

Middlesbrough midfielder Sebastian Berhalter said: 'He's meant so much to me and he's helped me develop as a player and as a person. And as a player, that's all you can ask for, to have that trust and have that belief in you.'

But not every player in the system was tripping over themselves to play under Poch. Just ask Christian Pulisic, who took the entire summer off in 2025 to rest before the World Cup – only to put up a goose egg in his home country.

Any hope for further progress under Pochettino evaporated when United came calling

All of this being said, there was reason for hope in the future. By re-signing Pochettino, the chance to cement that work ethic, culture and leadership presented itself.

With his extension, Pochettino had the chance to build a foundation in US Soccer to engender future success for decades to come.

Now, that's all gone. Now, Pochettino's time in charge will be remembered more for unfulfilled potential than culture shifting. After all, how do you expect to keep a culture if its chief architect leaves?

US Soccer now is faced with a quagmire of either hiring the biggest possible name again (Guardiola, if you believe the rumors) or hiring someone who will treat the position less like a stepping stone and more like a cornerstone.

It never seemed like Pochettino fully embraced the US, despite the tears on Friday. He'll be off for Old Trafford and a United squad bogged down by perpetual disappointment, all while leaving behind the biggest "What If" in the still-growing history of the American game.

#1850. Who can England face in Nations League draw? Dream and nightmare scenario revealed

England will learn their opponents for the Nations League quarter-finals on Friday morning.

The Three Lions beat Spain in dramatic circumstances in Madrid to top their group last week, and can now avoid the likes of France, Germany and Portugal in the quarter-finals as a result.

But the draw might still throw up some tricky fixtures as England look to improve on their best-ever finish in this competition, which came when they crossed the line in third in 2019.

Here is all you need to know about their potential opponents...

England are in Pot 1 for the Nations League draw, along with France, Germany and Portugal.

The teams in Pot 2 are Belgium, Spain, the Netherlands and Norway.

The Nations League draw will pit each of the four teams in Pot 1 against one of those in Pot 2, for a two-legged quarter-final.

There is one provision, though: teams from the same group cannot be drawn against each other, meaning England cannot face Spain at this stage of the competition. They could, however, come across them in the semi-finals or final.

As such, England could draw Belgium, the Netherlands, or Norway in the quarter-final.

Semi-final matchups will be determined by another draw following the quarter-finals.

England’s dream opponent at this stage of the Nations League is Norway.

FIFA sees Martin Odegaard and Erling Haaland’s side as comfortably the lowest-ranked of England’s three potential opponents.

That is in spite of their impressive World Cup campaign - where they were knocked out in the quarter-finals by England - and the fact they turned over both Denmark and Wales in the November international break.

England’s nightmare draw, meanwhile, would see them pitted against Belgium.

It is tough to say whether Belgium or the Netherlands would be the tougher opponent at this stage - FIFA ranks them at eighth and ninth in the world, respectively - but the Red Devils just pip their neighbours.

They finished second in their group, just a single point off winners France. A pair of one-sided victories over Turkiye and Italy got them to this stage.

The quarter-final first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The semi-finals and final will be played in June 2027.

#1849. Barnsley vs Sheffield Wednesday - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 18 Nov 2026 17:17

Barnsley will welcome Sheffield Wednesday to Oakwell on Friday for a South Yorkshire Derby of major importance at both ends of the League One table.

The visitors moved up to fifth spot with a return to winning ways under new management last weekend, while their visitors sit 23rd in the midst of a winless run in the third tier.

Barnsley head into a South Yorkshire Derby on Friday aiming to end a poor run of League One form and climb towards safety.

From their 13 league matches so far this season, since the summer return of former promotion-winning manager Daniel Stendel, they have picked up just nine points, winning just two and losing eight of those.

The most recent of those victories came at the beginning of September, and the Reds have gone winless in nine third-tier matches since, having gone into a meeting with fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic last weekend with fresh optimism on the back of a draw against Oxford United and consecutive cup victories.

They failed to convert those results into an elusive league win, though, leaving the Brick Community Stadium empty-handed following a 2-1 defeat, as Cameron McGeehan cancelled Fraser Murray's opener out on the hour mark, only for Jensen Weir to put the hosts back ahead 15 minutes from time.

Now three points adrift of safety and only above basement side Bromley on goal difference, Barnsley will be desperate to begin reversing their fortunes with a win over their rivals on Friday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the short trip aiming to make it consecutive league victories under new management to climb closer to the top two.

After a positive start to life back in League One, with fresh ownership, a new and improved squad and their sights set on a return to the Championship, Sheffield Wednesday hit a tougher spell across October and early November with consecutive losses spelling the end of Henrik Pedersen's tenure.

Consecutive draws then followed under caretaker management, leaving the Owls on 20 points from 13 games after a fast start, before they turned to new manager Dave Challinor, whose tenure started with consecutive cup defeats at the hands of fourth-tier Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley.

Saturday then brought about a first league game as Owls boss for Challinor, and he oversaw a first victory at Hillsborough in style as the South Yorkshire outfit leapfrogged their visitors with a 3-0 triumph thanks to Billy Mitchell's opener and goals from Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard in the final 10 minutes.

Now hoping to be out of their brief slump and with fresh optimism under their new boss, Sheffield Wednesday find themselves fifth and six points off the automatic promotion places and will bid to keep building momentum with a second straight win on Friday.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):

Barnsley remain without defender Jack Shepherd, while key midfielder and captain Cameron McGeehan is also out suspended after reaching five yellow cards for the season last time out.

Fabio Jalo and Ben Hamed Toure are out injured, while Patrick Kelly is back in contention after being away on international duty and will come back into the midfield.

Kelly will replace McGeehan and could join Luca Connell and Daniel Johnson in the midfield, while Reyes Cleary and Vimal Yoganathan will again support a lone striker with Makenzie Kirk, Rylan Brownlie and Amani Richards competing to lead the line.

Sheffield Wednesday may be unchanged from last week's impressive 3-0 victory, having seen their injury troubles eased recently with Liam Cooper, Bernard, Mitchell, first-choice goalkeeper Joe Lumley and danger man Louie Barry all back available.

Ali Al-Hamadi, Kieran Morrison and Jordi Liongola are also in contention, with Mason Burstow still out, while Barry may be eased back in after a long layoff with Barry Bannan and Callum Slattery likely to continue supporting front man Keillor-Dunn, who has scored in each of his last three appearances.

Elsewhere, Bernard and Cooper should again be joined by Sil Swinkels in a back three, while they are light on the left-hand side with Reece James and Max Lowe out of action alongside Burstow.

Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche; Johnson, Connell; Yoganathan, Kelly, Cleary; Kirk

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Valery, Heskey, Mitchell, Gray; Slattery, Bannan; Keillor-Dunn

Sheffield Wednesday looked somewhat back to their best in last weekend's beating of fellow promotion-chasers Plymouth Argyle, and we fancy them to make it consecutive clean sheets and wins against a Barnsley side devoid of confidence and without top scorer McGeehan.

#1848. Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”

The final whistle is blown at the Emirates and Arsenal maintain their 100% record through three games as they have beaten Chelsea 2-1. They were 1-0 down inside the opening two minutes but goals from Havertz and Odegaard have led them to victory. Chelsea suffer their first competitive defeat under Xabi Alonso.

Pedro’s cross from the right has too much on it and Chavarria cannot head it back across goal. Chelsea’s last chance might have been that Estevao effort which was brilliantly saved by Raya.

That is a stunning save from Raya that may have preserved Arsenal’s victory. Estevao cuts in from the right and curls one towards the top corner. It looks set for the net but somehow Raya makes a fantastic save to deny Estevao.

Although he hasn’t yet.

England team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a big club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. He plays the ball inside towards Havertz, who is in space on the edge of the Chelsea box. Tremendous game at the Emirates. Both teams attacking one another. Chelsea have a lot of space with Pedro Neto on the right and keep using that diagonal ball. Former Chelsea player scores against former Arsenal goalkeeper. Interesting reaction from the Arsenal players to that Havertz goal: most of them ran straight back to their own half. They want to get on with this game. Suggests they can sense Chelsea’s vulnerability.

Against his former club, Havertz gets the equaliser but again there will be an offside check. It appears he is onside as he receives the ball on the right. For Liverpool, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Spain, Alonso was one of the finest midfielders of his generation and also played with some of the best midfielders in the world. So the Chelsea manager knows a thing or two about what it takes.

James has long been considered – when fit – one of the best right-backs in the world. But it had already been evident before the final 24 hours of the transfer window that the Chelsea player would spend a lot of time in midfield under Alonso.

Bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. Failure to secure a big-name forward has led many to conclude that Arsenal’s title defence will be in the mould of their impressive, but cautious 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”

A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. They have just got back under way in the second half on Merseyside and Manchester United have taken the lead against Everton through Bryan Mbeumo. You can follow the action from the Hill Dickinson here.

Will Ezri Konsa come into Arsenal’s starting lineup today? It would be harsh on Cristhian Mosquera, who has been excellent so far this season, but when you pay more than £50m for a ready-made, elite-level centre-back, these are the matches you surely want him for. Mosquera had a slight injury against Aston Villa on Monday night, which may give Arteta the perfect reason to throw his new signing into the side.

Today:Everton 0 Manchester United 0 HTArsenal vs Chelsea 4.30pm

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.
