#1847. Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

With promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

Rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

At times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

#1846. Leeds confirm huge injury boost for Chelsea clash as two stars return

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Daniel Farke expects to have Anton Stach in the squad when Leeds visit Chelsea on Saturday.

The Blues have only won one of their last three league outings, with defeats by Sunderland and Tottenham coming either side of a 2-0 victory over Manchester United, but have their work cut out for them if they are to get back to winning ways sa they host Farke’s Leeds.

Stach has proven influential since moving to Yorkshire last summer, with his performances enough to earn him a spot in the national team.

He was forced to miss the home defeat of Tottenham earlier this month, however, with a broken toe.

But Farke has hinted his countryman will be back in the fold for the trip to Stamford Bridge, having spent the past week training with his team-mates.

"He [Stach] was a full week back in training, today,” Farke explained at his pre-match press conference. “Last week, still a bit like part integrated and a bit of individual rehab work.”

That leaves Farke with a fully-fit squad for the trip down to west London, a considerable boost for his chances. of picking up three points.

Chelsea, meanwhile, remain injury-hit. It is not yet clear whether Joao Pedro will be available to return from his own injury, while Moises Caicedo has also picked up an issue on international duty.

Reece James is in recovery from knee surgery, with centre-back Maxence Lacroix also out until the new year.

#1845. Hansi Flick finds unexpected Frenkie De Jong solution

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 17:18, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 17:29

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick may have found an unexpected way to accommodate Frenkie de Jong in his increasingly competitive squad, with the Netherlands international demonstrating his value in an unfamiliar position during the club's recent victory over Atletico Madrid.

The 29-year-old has endured another injury-disrupted year, while the arrival of Rodri has added further competition to a midfield already featuring Pedri, Gavi, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo.

Yet De Jong's performance in Barcelona's 2-1 comeback victory over Atletico on November 8 offered a reminder of why Flick continues to regard him as an important member of his squad.

Introduced at half-time with Barcelona trailing, the Dutchman was surprisingly deployed at right-back rather than in his customary midfield role.

The decision helped Barcelona gain control of possession and establish a stronger presence in the opposition half, with De Jong eventually returning to central midfield following another tactical adjustment.

His influence was reflected in the statistics: he completed 65 of his 67 passes, achieving an accuracy rate of 97%, despite playing only 45 minutes.

For a player who has repeatedly faced questions about his future at the Camp Nou, it was another example of how his particular qualities can provide solutions beyond the position traditionally associated with him.

Flick's decision to introduce De Jong at right-back was particularly significant given Barcelona's difficulties in controlling the first half against Diego Simeone's side.

The German manager replaced Brian Farinas with the former Ajax midfielder, who offered a very different interpretation of the position.

Rather than remaining close to the touchline, De Jong frequently moved into central areas when Barcelona had possession, helping his teammates progress the ball through Atletico's pressure.

His ability to receive under pressure, turn away from opponents and carry possession forward allowed Barcelona to build attacks without relying exclusively on passes from their defenders.

That mobility has been one of De Jong's defining qualities throughout his career, although his contribution does not always translate into goals or assists.

According to Mundo Deportivo, he completed 22 passes in the attacking third against Atletico, more than any other Barcelona player, despite spending the entire first half on the bench.

Barcelona's overall possession increased from 58% before the interval to 68% in the second half, during which they registered 10 attempts on goal and allowed just two.

Those improvements cannot be attributed solely to De Jong, but his introduction provided a technical outlet that had been missing earlier in the contest.

Flick subsequently moved the Dutchman back into midfield after Eric Garcia entered the match, illustrating another advantage of having a player comfortable in several positions.

De Jong has previously been used as a central defender and in more advanced midfield roles, while his experience in Barcelona's build-up play makes him particularly effective when moving between the defensive and midfield lines.

The Atletico performance offered further evidence that his versatility can be valuable even when he is not an automatic starter in his preferred position.

De Jong's situation has changed considerably since the summer of 2022, when Manchester United pursued his signature under former Ajax manager Erik ten Hag.

Barcelona were prepared to consider his departure during a period of significant financial difficulties, but the midfielder remained determined to continue his career in Catalonia.

His relationship with the club has subsequently been complicated by questions over deferred wages, recurring injuries and speculation surrounding his importance to successive managers.

Nevertheless, Barcelona demonstrated their commitment to the Dutchman by extending his contract until June 2029 in October last year.

The renewal came despite his difficult injury history, which included the ankle problems that ruled him out of Euro 2024.

He suffered another major setback during the 2026 World Cup, sustaining a knee ligament injury that prevented him from featuring during the opening months of the current campaign.

De Jong eventually returned against Real Madrid on October 25 and recently reached 300 competitive appearances for Barcelona.

However, the arrival of Rodri has created an additional selection challenge for Flick.

The Spanish international offers a more natural defensive presence at the base of midfield, while Pedri remains central to Barcelona's ability to dictate possession and create opportunities.

Gavi, Bernal, Fermin and Olmo provide further alternatives, leaving Flick with considerable flexibility but difficult decisions whenever his midfielders are fit.

De Jong's capacity to operate in several roles could therefore prove particularly useful, especially when Barcelona need additional composure during the early stages of their attacking moves.

His ability to advance with the ball also offers something different from Rodri's positional discipline and Pedri's creativity between the lines.

That does not necessarily mean De Jong will become a regular right-back. His appearance against Atletico was a tactical response to the circumstances of a particular match rather than confirmation of a permanent positional change.

There is also the continuing question of his fitness.

De Jong withdrew from the Netherlands squad during the November international break after experiencing muscular discomfort, although Barcelona subsequently confirmed that the problem was not serious.

The midfielder is expected to be available for Sunday's La Liga encounter with Villarreal, providing Flick with another important option as Rodri continues his recovery from a hamstring injury.

After years in which De Jong was frequently discussed as a potential departure, his recent performances have underlined why Barcelona have been reluctant to give up on him.

His future role may depend less on securing one fixed position in Flick's midfield than on his ability to perform several functions within the same game.

#1844. Manchester United XI vs Liverpool: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Premier League

Mauricio Pochettino will pick his first Manchester United team on Sunday for a daunting debut away at Liverpool.

As such, wholesale changes from life under Carrick are not forecast, at least in terms of setup. After all, both managers have a penchant for the same 4-2-3-1 formation.

A midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo will sit behind the trio of Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

Patrick Dorgu is expected to be fit, too, but it remains to be seen whether he can unseat Matheus Cunha off the left. He could also deputise Shaw if his fitness levels are not up to par.

#1842. Tottenham women confirm executive shake-up as new sporting director appointed

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham have confirmed the appointment of a new director of women’s football, which comes as part of a thorough shake-up of the team’s management.

Kim Pedersen will take over the running of Spurs women from December 7, joining from Danish side Brondby.

He will bring to north London nearly 15 years of experience in football coaching and administration, across both the men’s and women’s game. In his most recent role, the Norwegian helped Brondby become Denmark’s first fully professional women’s outfit.

He joins a Tottenham side on something of an upward trajectory. The club has been steadily improving since the appointment of Martin Ho last year and has a clear aspiration to qualify for the Champions League, though they look set to fall short of that target this term despite heavy investment in the summer transfer window.

Pedersen’s appointment comes some six months on from the departure of the long-serving Andy Rogers, formerly managing director of the women’s team, whose 24-year spell with the club ended in May.

Speaking in an interview with the club after signing, Pedersen set his sights on helping Tottenham to upset the WSL’s heavyweights.

Also joining Tottenham women alongside Pedersen are Lucy Button, newly appointed the women’s growth director, and Hannah Sheridan, the women’s director of performance and operations.

Tottenham’s director of football operations Rafi Moersen said: “We have made a deliberate decision to evolve the way we lead Women's football at Tottenham Hotspur, establishing dedicated leadership across three critical areas: football, performance and operations, and commercial growth.

“This is about building the foundations for sustained success, on and off the pitch, with clear accountability, specialist leadership and the ambition to accelerate our progress.

“Together, these appointments, alongside continued investment in our infrastructure, represent an important step in our commitment to building a successful and sustainable future for Women's football at Tottenham Hotspur.”

#1841. Declan Rice bites back at Graeme Souness: Arsenal star claims pundit doesn't understand how the game has evolved over 'old man's football' criticism - and jokes: 'My numbers aren't bad "for a centre-back!"'

Published: 15:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 15:40 EST, 14 November 2026

Declan Rice has laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness by claiming his numbers 'aren't bad for a centre back', after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' and 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Souness has long believed the Arsenal and England star does not do enough for a midfielder and said recently he might as well play centre back, adding that he would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Rice is aware of what Souness has said but believes his return of 22 goals and 33 assists since joining the Gunners in 2023 disproves the former Liverpool midfielder's opinion.

‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves,’ said Rice. ‘For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’

Rice, who will start as an advanced midfielder when England take on Spain here in Madrid on Sunday night, added: ‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’

Rice also believes Souness, 73, may not understand how the game has evolved.

England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has laughed off Graeme Souness' criticism after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' 'cheating' by dropping into defence

Pundit Souness believes Rice would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man's football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ began Rice. 'We played him the other week and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball. The game is different now. It's what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It's changed a lot, and you're always trying to look for tactical advantages.

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I'm constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He's constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we're now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There's no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he's done.

‘I didn't get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I've never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’

#1840. GdS: Worth the price tag – how Moreira became ‘untouchable’ for Milan and Belgium

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby shows, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

He set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Moreira is currently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

With four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

#1838. Revealed: Matthias Jaissle’s eleventh-hour bid to stop Bruno Guimaraes’ Arsenal switch

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Matthias Jaissle made a last-ditch attempt to convince Bruno Guimaraes to snub offers from Arsenal and stay at Newcastle.

Guimaraes signed for Arsenal in a £75m deal in August - just three days after Jaissle’s appointment as Eddie Howe’s replacement - calling time on a four-year association with Newcastle, where he was a favourite of the club’s passionate fanbase.

The Magpies were desperate to keep Guimaraes on Tyneside and dug their heels in to prevent the deal, but eventually gave in once it became clear the player had set his heart on the transfer. He has since scored twice in 14 appearances for the Gunners.

#1837. Real Madrid: Vini Jr "hasn't been the same" since this one star name left

By Ben Knapton | 18 Nov 2026 17:46

Vinicius Junior's struggles at Real Madrid have as much to do with the departure of Toni Kroos as the arrival of Kylian Mbappe, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.

The Brazilian ended 2026 on a high for his country, scoring twice in Saturday's 3-2 friendly defeat to Japan before hitting a first-half hat-trick in Tuesday's 7-0 rout of Singapore, his first treble for the Selecao.

Those five goals offered a stark contrast to his club form; Vinicius managed just one goal for Real Madrid before the first international break of 2026-27, and he was then handed a four-match La Liga ban for pulling the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba, ruling him out of El Clasico.

Speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, Vickery suggested that restoring the forward's confidence had been one of Carlo Ancelotti's main objectives for the window, while pointing to an issue that has received little attention.

"From the moment Mbappe was signed by Real Madrid, how do you fit the two of them together, both in tactical and temperamental terms?" Vickery said.

"Vini had been the main man. He'd won them Champions Leagues. Mbappe comes in and he's almost promoted above him as the star turn.

"They both like to retreat and attack from that space wide on the left. That was always going to be difficult, and it has proved difficult.

"But there's one thing that is possibly even more important, and I haven't seen many people talk about it: the loss of Toni Kroos. I think it's no coincidence that Vini hasn't been the same player since."

Kroos retired after Euro 2024, the same summer in which Mbappe arrived from Paris Saint-Germain, and Vickery believes the absence of a midfield conductor is now hurting Vinicius for both club and country.

"You can't really win the game down the flanks without having some kind of control in the centre of midfield," he added.

"That's been Ancelotti's problem with Brazil so far as he tries to get the best out of Vini, and I think that's Vini's problem with Real Madrid as well.

"He was so much a better player when he had the passing range of Toni Kroos as his supply line. I don't know how Real Madrid are going to solve that one."

Vinicius will now return to Jose Mourinho's side ahead of Saturday's La Liga meeting with Celta Vigo, hoping his international goal spree can spark a revival. However, Vickery's assessment suggests a lasting solution may depend on Real Madrid's recruitment in the centre of the park, rather than on the Brazilian alone.

#1836. How to watch Nations League draw: TV channel and live stream for today

England are set to discover their route to the Nations League final this morning, as the quarter-final draw is made in Nyon, Switzerland.

The Three Lions finished atop their group to ensure their status as one of eight teams to have qualified for the knockout rounds of the competition, capping their group-stage campaign with a statement 3-2 defeat of Spain in Madrid.

They saw out that last win in dramatic fashion, clinging on with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent for an early shower after a cynical foul on Lamine Yamal.

Thomas Tuchel’s men will be joined in the quarter-finals by the world champions, La Roja, as well as the likes of France, Germany, and the Netherlands.

Cristiano Ronaldo-less Portugal, Belgium, and Norway make up the numbers. The quarter-finals will be staged next March, with the final, which may yet be hosted at Wembley Stadium, pencilled in for the summer of 2027.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place today, Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

#1834. Di Marzio: Endrick and Tresoldi deals ‘not a financial issue’ for Milan – the situation

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

“That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

“We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

“But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”

#1833. Lampard: Decisions went against Coventry in defeat to Everton

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Frank Lampard was still left questioning the decisions made during Coventry City's 3-1 defeat to Everton as they prepare to bounce back against Crystal Palace on Saturday.

Coventry signed off for the international break with a loss at Hill Dickinson Stadium, despite taking the lead through Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute strike past Jordan Pickford.

However, Thierno Barry led Everton's fightback with two goals before teeing up Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, though Lampard expressed his confusion about some of the decisions.

And on Wednesday, the independent Key Match Incidents panel concluded that Coventry should have been awarded a penalty when James Tarkowski fouled Caleb Yirenkyi.

There was also wide-scale debate over Thierno Barry's second goal and whether it was handball, with the Everton forward squeezing the ball in at Carl Rushworth's near post.

"It's a game we lost because of decisions, in my opinion," Lampard told reporters of those findings. "There were decisions that went wrongly against us by the referee.

"I appreciate they were honest after the event, but that doesn't help us. Going away from home is not easy, but I felt like we deserved a result. We must keep going.

"These things happen in football so we have to keep positive and keep going."

Thank you for your support on the road this evening, safe travels home. https://t.co/FFMkr8xTAh

— Coventry City (@CoventryCityFC) November 6, 2026

There will be a new face in the Palace dugout at the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend, with Thomas Frank set to take charge of his first game with the Eagles.

Frank was appointed as Palace's new boss following the sacking of Pierre Sage, who left the club sitting bottom of the Premier League after 10 matches.

Only two of Palace's 13 previous permanent managers in the Premier League have won their first game in charge (D4 L7 – first spells only), with Alan Pardew beating Tottenham in January 2015 and Oliver Glasner beating Burnley in February 2024.

And when asked about his hopes for the rest of the season, Frank outlined his ambition to help Palace compete on all fronts, including the EFL Cup and Europa League.

"Of course, I've looked at the team and done a lot of analysis on the team. I think there's a lot of positives, definitely," Frank said.

"There's no doubt, to state the obvious, that we need to stabilise things. That's one thing. We need to work incredibly hard.

"Obviously, we're conceding too many goals that we need to address, so we need to work on the defensive side of things with principles, attitude, everything regarding that.

"Then, of course, it's one game at a time. We need to balance a lot of things with aiming high in Europe. There are two fantastic cup tournaments, but, of course, the Premier League is the most important, if we need to prioritise. But we would like to compete on all fronts."

Rudoni is one of six players who are both their team's leading shot taker (17) and chance creator (17) in the top-flight this season, alongside Chelsea's Cole Palmer, Palace's Yeremy Pino, Ipswich Town's Julio Enciso, Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes, and Newcastle United's Harvey Barnes.

He is also the only Coventry City player to score more than once in the Premier League this season (three).

Despite falling to a 3-1 defeat against Liverpool ahead of the international break, one positive for Palace was to see Nketiah get himself on the scoresheet.

Nketiah scored his first goal in the Premier League this season, netting for the first time since December 2025 against Fulham, and with Jean-Philippe Mateta still serving a suspension, Frank could give him the nod up front ahead of Jorgen Strand Larsen.

— Crystal Palace F.C. (@CPFC) November 16, 2026

This is the first meeting between Coventry and Crystal in any competition since March 2012, a 1-1 draw in the Championship.

Coventry have lost just one of their six Premier League games against Palace (W2 D3), with this the first meeting since a 3-0 win at Selhurst Park in February 1998.

The Sky Blues have, however, lost seven or more of their opening 10 games of a league campaign for only the third time ever, also doing so in their first two Football League seasons in 1919-20 (nine) and 1920-21 (seven). It is already as many defeats as they suffered in last season's Championship.

But they face a Palace side that have conceded 24 goals in 10 Premier League games this season, their most at this stage of a season since 1980-81 under Terry Venables (also 24).

Indeed, 10 of the 15 sides to have conceded that many goals in their first 10 Premier League games have been relegated, though Wolves did it most recently in 2024-25 (27 conceded) and ended the season in 16th.

Palace won their first four visits to the Coventry Building Society Arena between 2005 and 2008 but are winless in their last four in all competitions between 2009 and 2012 (D2 L2), making Frank's debut all the more tricky.

#1832. Mauricio Pochettino's first words at Tottenham, PSG, Chelsea and USA reveal Man United approach

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 19:40

Mauricio Pochettino has officially begun his Manchester United reign, but his first press conferences at Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States offer a revealing insight into how he intends to tackle the crisis at Old Trafford.

The Argentine arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, November 18, having completed his final international assignment with the United States, and faces an immediate challenge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

United sit 18th in the Premier League after winning just one of their opening 10 matches, with Michael Carrick's dismissal leaving Pochettino responsible for restoring confidence to a squad struggling for results.

The 54-year-old has inherited troubled teams before, although few appointments have offered such little preparation time before a fixture of this magnitude.

Looking back at his opening statements in four previous jobs reveals a recurring approach: Pochettino tends to publicly back the players he inherits, avoid making immediate transfer demands and emphasise the importance of collective responsibility.

Those principles have helped him transform some teams, but his experiences at PSG and Chelsea also demonstrate that they do not guarantee success.

When Pochettino arrived at Tottenham in 2014, the club were searching for stability after a disappointing campaign under Andre Villas-Boas and Tim Sherwood.

The Argentine had built his reputation at Southampton, where his energetic pressing system and ability to develop young players attracted considerable attention.

At his first major press engagement with Spurs, he resisted suggestions that widespread recruitment was necessary.

"We have an unbelievable squad with unbelievable players," Pochettino insisted.

"The most important thing is to develop our players and to provide the best team to play on the pitch."

His message was clear: improving the existing squad would take priority over demanding new signings.

That approach eventually helped Tottenham establish themselves among the Premier League's leading clubs.

Pochettino guided Spurs to second place in 2016-17 and reached the Champions League final in 2019, although he departed later that year without winning a trophy.

His appointment at PSG in January 2021 presented a different challenge.

Rather than developing a relatively young Premier League squad, Pochettino inherited a team containing established superstars, including Neymar and Kylian Mbappe.

During his introductory press conference, the Argentine again rejected the idea of imposing a rigid tactical system regardless of the available personnel.

Discussing the roles of Neymar and Mbappe, he explained that his responsibility was to find positions in which they could express their abilities and become decisive.

He also emphasised that a team's behaviour with and without possession mattered more than the formation displayed on paper.

The flexibility he promised was tested by the demands of managing an exceptionally talented squad.

Although PSG won Ligue 1 in 2021-22, Pochettino failed to deliver the Champions League success the club wanted and departed that summer.

Chelsea offered another rebuilding assignment in 2023.

The Blues had finished 12th in the Premier League after a turbulent campaign, and Pochettino was tasked with restoring their competitiveness following extensive changes to the playing squad.

At his first press conference, he acknowledged that performances alone would not satisfy expectations at Stamford Bridge.

The Argentine also expressed confidence in the club's sporting structure, explaining that he had accepted the owners' strategic plan rather than seeking greater authority over recruitment.

His Chelsea side eventually recovered to finish sixth and reached the EFL Cup final, but an inconsistent campaign ended with his departure by mutual consent in May 2024.

The experience demonstrated the difficulty of introducing a long-term playing philosophy while facing pressure for immediate results.

Pochettino's introductory press conference with the United States in September 2024 provided perhaps the clearest indication of the demands United's players can expect.

The former Tottenham manager made collective effort central to his philosophy, insisting that individual talent would only be effective within a properly organised team.

"But when we don't have the ball, we need to run, we need to be aggressive, we need to be competitive," he explained.

He also stressed that his coaching staff needed to create an environment in which players understood their responsibilities and could express their abilities.

That message carries particular relevance at Old Trafford.

United have conceded 19 goals in their opening 10 Premier League matches and have struggled to produce the collective intensity required to compete consistently.

Pochettino's preference for coordinated pressing could offer one route towards improvement, although implementing those principles will require time and careful management of the squad's physical condition.

His previous appointments suggest that he is unlikely to begin by publicly criticising individual players or demanding a major January overhaul.

At Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea, his introductory message focused on working with the players already available, with recruitment generally left to the club's decision-makers.

That approach may be particularly important at United, where the relationship between the head coach and the sporting department will come under scrutiny as the January transfer window approaches.

Pochettino also has a record of improving young players, an asset for a squad featuring talents such as Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo and Benjamin Sesko.

However, the circumstances surrounding his arrival leave little opportunity for a gradual introduction.

Unlike at Chelsea, where he benefited from a full pre-season, the Argentine has only a handful of training sessions before facing Liverpool.

United's position in the relegation zone also creates a more urgent challenge than the long-term projects he initially discussed at Tottenham or with the United States.

His opening press conferences across those four jobs suggest he will seek to protect his players publicly while demanding greater effort and discipline behind the scenes.

Whether those familiar principles can produce an immediate response will become clearer at Anfield, where Pochettino faces one of the most difficult possible introductions to life as Manchester United manager.

#1831. Nottingham Forest: 21-year-old transfer target could be "eaten up" in Premier League

By Ben Knapton | 18 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 20:30

Nottingham Forest target Gabriel Morais Silva Bontempo is not yet ready for the Premier League, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.

The Santos midfielder has reportedly been tracked by Forest for much of 2026, with Oliver Glasner's side weighing up a move in the January transfer window. Bournemouth are also said to be interested.

Bontempo, who turns 22 in January, has enjoyed a breakthrough year, contributing six goals and five assists in 50 appearances, and he earned his first Brazil call-up in September.

The lynchpin's contract runs until 2030, though, and speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, Vickery expressed doubts over whether the youngster could handle the step up to English football.

"He's had to grow up very quickly as a central midfielder with Santos," Vickery said. "His first year was a prolonged battle against relegation, and it is a team full of veterans, which puts a lot of strain on a young midfielder.

"He really has to cover the ground and link the play. He's a good little give-and-go midfielder.

"Premier League, now I have my doubts. He's around the six-foot mark, so he's not small, but he is physically quite flimsy.

"Everyone who comes from South American football to the Premier League says the same thing: 'You've got to play quicker. You must know what you're going to do with the ball before it comes.'

"In a Premier League midfield, I think he could be eaten up. I wouldn't see him as a player who's Premier League ready at the moment."

Rather than Bontempo, Vickery believes Forest should consider a familiar face in Danilo.

The 25-year-old broke his ankle on the opening day of the 2024-25 season against Bournemouth, and he joined Botafogo the following summer in a club-record deal worth around €22m (£19.2m).

Danilo was in superb form during the first half of 2026 and earned a place in Brazil's World Cup squad, but his hopes of securing a move to a Premier League side playing in the Champions League have yet to materialise.

"Forest could do a lot worse than get the left-footed, strong, quick-thinking, versatile Danilo back," Vickery added.

"At the moment, he's a better bet than Gabriel Bontempo, who is certainly one for the long term rather than now."

Danilo scored six goals and set up four more in 10 appearances for Nottingham Forest and was also linked with Manchester United during the summer transfer window.

#1830. Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision with Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel given 12-MATCH ban - and may never return to football

Published: 16:25 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:42 EST, 14 November 2026

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been sanctioned after a horrifying foul with Tenerife's De Miguel earlier this month.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned with De Miguel, 30, admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

The goalkeeper was subjected to chants of 'murderer' by Tenerife supporters and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash.

Now his manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so].

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games and could quit football for good after he collided with Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel, who died

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as the keeper attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'

Earlier this month, Owono issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Police are investigating the death of De Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response

Owono said he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.'

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'

'There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

#1829. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1828. Man Utd transfer news: £66.8m Arsenal and Chelsea target sends 'timely reminder' to Mauricio Pochettino

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 00:19

Nico Paz is reportedly set to spark a tussle for his signature after Mauricio Pochettino's recent appointment at Manchester United.

The 22-year-old Como midfielder stole the show in Argentina's recent emphatic 7-0 friendly rout of Costa Rica during the international break.

Paz opened the scoring with a thunderous long-range strike into the top corner before leaving two defenders in his wake and firing home a powerful effort with his weaker foot to make it 3-0.

Fellow compatriots Julian Alvarez and 19-year-old Fiorentina loanee Franco Mastantuono also struck doubles during the dominant international display.

United supporters are already painfully familiar with the playmaker's long-range prowess after a carbon-copy strike sparked Como's 4-1 Champions League demolition of the Red Devils last month.

According to The Sun, Pochettino's recent arrival in the Old Trafford dugout could hand Manchester United a decisive advantage in their pursuit of his fellow Argentine.

Paz has established himself as one of European football's most coveted young prospects this term, contributing six goals and eight assists to register a direct goal involvement every 81 minutes.

Standing at 6ft 1in, the attacking midfielder combines refined technical quality with the physical resilience required to withstand the relentless intensity of the Premier League.

However, the source above states that prying the former Real Madrid Castilla graduate away from Serie A will prove complicated given that Los Blancos retain an €80m (£66.8m) option to re-sign him in 2027.

United also reportedly face fierce competition from across the continent, with Premier League rivals Arsenal and Chelsea alongside Paris Saint-Germain all closely monitoring his rapid progression.

The source above believes that Pochettino should receive substantial financial backing from the club hierarchy when the winter transfer window opens in January.

While adding a dynamic playmaker of Paz's calibre remains an enticing long-term objective, the Red Devils are initially expected to prioritise recruiting a new striker and a defender.

The need for defensive reinforcements has grown increasingly urgent amid reports that Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez wants out of Old Trafford despite earning plaudits for his recent international displays.
