#1826. Premier League predictions: Pochettino starts life at Man Utd against rivals Liverpool

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

The Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of the latest weekend of the 2026-27 Premier League season following the latest international break.

During the two-week hiatus, there were two managerial changes, with Mauricio Pochettino replacing Michael Carrick at Manchester United, who sit in the relegation zone, and Thomas Frank succeeding Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace, who prop up the table.

At the other end of the standings, Arsenal hold a five-point lead, having won each of their last five matches.

They sit above high-flying Brighton, while Manchester City slipped down to third following three straight losses.

Matchday 11 sees fixtures take place on Saturday, Sunday and Monday, and ahead of what should be another enticing group of Premier League fixtures, we check out the Opta supercomputer's match predictions.

Manchester City's strong start to the season came crashing down before the break, and they are looking to get back to winning ways when they host Fulham on Saturday.

City have lost three straight league games, as many as in their previous 36 (W25 D8); since the start of 2007-08, they have only lost four in a row twice, doing so in August 2008 and December 2024.

However, City have won their last 17 Premier League games against Fulham and have won their last 20 against the Cottagers in all competitions.

— Manchester City (@ManCity) November 17, 2026

And our predictive model makes them the favourites to triumph at 66.1%, with no team having a higher win probability across the fixtures this weekend. Fulham's hopes of a win sit at 15.5%.

Fulham struggled at the start of the season, but they are unbeaten in their last four league games (W2 D2) and have lost just one of their last seven (W2 D4).

Onto the 15:00 kick-offs, Aston Villa are looking to bounce back after throwing away a late lead in their thrilling 4-4 draw with Man Utd against Sunderland.

Villa have lost just one of their last 12 top-flight matches against Sunderland (W5 D6), going down 3-1 at the Stadium of Light in January 2016.

And Villa are unbeaten in their last six league games (W3 D3), though they dropped points from winning positions in all three draws.

Sunderland, meanwhile, are looking to win successive Premier League games for the first time this season following their 1-0 victory over Chelsea last time out.

It is Villa who are the favourites to triumph, winning 59.3% of the supercomputer's pre-match simulations for Unai Emery's 150th league game in charge, to Sunderland's 19.4%.

A rampant Bournemouth (55.3%) are looking to continue their push up the table against Nottingham Forest (21.6%), who ended their slump against Man City before the break.

The Cherries, who have won each of their last eight matches in all competitions, are unbeaten in all eight of their Premier League games against Forest (W4 D4).

Bournemouth have pushed their way into the top seven after a slow start to the campaign, and they are now aiming to win five straight games in the top-flight for the very first time.

As for Forest, they are winless in six league away games against Bournemouth (D2 L4), though they are looking to win successive top-flight matches for the second time this calendar year (a run of three in April/May).

And a victory would be the perfect result for Oliver Glasner, who is set to take charge of his 100th Premier League match (W33 D32 L34), though he is yet to beat Bournemouth in the competition.

Chelsea went into the international break after a disappointing loss to Sunderland, while Leeds United ended their five-game winless streak with a win over Tottenham.

The Blues are expected to come out on top at Stamford Bridge, with a 51.1% win probability, given they have won 10 points in five top-flight home games this term (W3 D1 L1).

Club football returns! https://t.co/KobVgRE0k4

— Leeds United (@LUFC) November 18, 2026

They have also won eight of their last 10 home games against Leeds in all competitions (D2), since a 2-0 loss in December 1999. Chelsea have already beaten the Whites at home in the EFL Cup this season, winning 6-3.

But Leeds, who won 24% of the pre-match simulations, avoided defeat in both league meetings with Chelsea in 2025-26 (3-1 at home, 2-2 away).

They have not gone three straight without defeat against them since between November 2000 and October 2001, however.

At 26.8%, there is a healthy chance of a draw between Coventry City and Crystal Palace, as Frank makes his bow in charge of the Eagles.

Coventry are the favourites, at 45.7%, while Palace have a 27.5% win probability.

This is the first meeting between Coventry and Palace in any competition since March 2012, a 1-1 draw in the Championship.

Palace won their first four visits to the Coventry Building Society Arena between 2005 and 2008 but are winless in their last four in all competitions between 2009 and 2012 (D2 L2).

Coventry have lost just one of their six Premier League games against Crystal Palace (W2 D3).

Frank's former club Tottenham are also in action on Saturday, as they host Ipswich Town.

Spurs' strong run was snapped in a 1-0 loss to Leeds before the international break, but our model is backing them to bounce back, with Roberto De Zerbi's team given a 55.2% win probability to Ipswich's 21.7%, with the chance of a draw coming in at 23.1%.

However, Spurs have lost four of their last five Premier League games against Ipswich, though the exception was a 4-1 win in their last meeting in February 2025.

Getting ready to be back on home turf @Betano_UK https://t.co/WowLWS0dPb

Tottenham are also winless in four when playing their first Premier League match after an international break (D1 L3), drawing 1-1 with Man Utd following this season's first break.

But Spurs should be expected to score, as Ipswich have conceded in each of their last 29 Premier League games, and only four teams have ever gone 30+ consecutive matches in the competition without a shutout.

Saturday's action rounds out at St. James' Park, as Newcastle United host Arsenal.

Newcastle have won just one of their last 29 Premier League games against sides starting the day top of the table (D8 L20), and none of their last 18 (D4 L14) since a 2-1 victory over Chelsea in December 2014.

And the supercomputer anticipates that run to continue, with Arsenal (56.4%) the most likely away victors this weekend.

None of Newcastle's last 13 Premier League home games against Arsenal have been drawn (W4 L9), with the Magpies winning three of the last five, but they are handed just a 21.7% win probability here.

Arsenal have only won more Premier League games against Everton (41) and West Ham (39) than they have against Newcastle (38), while their 32 clean sheets against the Magpies are the most one side has against another in the competition.

Hull City won their first two Premier League games this season but are winless in all eight since then (D5 L3).

It is the fourth time a side has won their first two games and then none of their next eight in the competition, along with Wolves in 2011-12, Hull in 2016-17, and West Brom in 2017-18, all of whom were relegated.

However, ahead of their first top-flight meeting with Brighton, the Tigers are still unbeaten at home in the Premier League this term.

Brighton are winless in all six of their visits to MKM Stadium in all competitions (D2 L4). Their last away win against Hull came at Boothferry Park in the fourth tier in October 2000.

But the Seagulls are flying high and are considered big favourites, at 50.1%. There is a 23.6% probability of a draw, with Hull's chances coming in at 26.3%.

Sunday's headline fixture sees Manchester United, under the tutelage of Pochettino, head to Anfield to face rivals, Liverpool.

Pochettino is the first United boss to see his first league game with the club come against Liverpool.

Your Manchester United head coach. https://t.co/9Bf8gBAj9s

Just one of the Red Devils' last nine bosses (including caretakers) has lost his first Premier League game of a spell in charge of the club (W4 D4), with Erik ten Hag losing 1-2 to Brighton in August 2022.

United won this fixture 2-1 last season, ending a nine-game winless run at Anfield in the Premier League (D5 L4).

In fact, Liverpool lost both Premier League meetings with United last season, as many as they had in their previous 18 (W7 D9). They last lost more consecutively between December 2014 and January 2016 (4).

But the supercomputer is backing Liverpool, who have a 57.3% win probability. United's chances are rated at just 20.5%, with a 22.2% draw threat.

MD11 rounds out with Brentford hosting Everton on Monday.

In-form Everton are the underdogs, with a 28.8% chance of winning. Brentford, meanwhile, are handed a 44.3% chance of victory. There is a 26.9% likelihood of a draw, making this game the most likely to finish all level.

Everton have won back-to-back Premier League games for the first time since February/March, and are looking to win three in a row in the competition for the first time since May 2025.

Brentford have won four of their last seven Premier League games at the Gtech Community Stadium (D2 L1), and are looking for back-to-back home league wins for the first time in 2026, having last done so in November 2025, when they won three on the spin.

#1825. Mauricio Pochettino's January plans at Man Utd face 'early test' as USMNT star speaks out on Old Trafford links

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 00:35

Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie is reportedly unlikely to seal a return to the Premier League during the upcoming January transfer window.

Speculation surrounding a potential mid-season switch to England intensified after the 28-year-old recently discussed the prospect of United States internationals reuniting with Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United.

Pochettino formally took the reins at Old Trafford following the dismissal of Michael Carrick, sparking immediate rumours that he could raid his former national team pool for winter reinforcements.

However, the Bianconeri have no intention of parting ways with the versatile American midway through the 2026-27 campaign.

According to Sky Sports News, Juventus head coach Luciano Spalletti is expected to publicly reiterate the club's firm stance against selling McKennie when he addresses the media this week.

The former Schalke man has remained an important figure in Turin this season, starting eight Serie A matches and contributing a goal alongside an assist in three Europa League outings.

McKennie is also understood to be completely settled in Italy after putting pen to paper on a lucrative contract extension in March that ties him to the Allianz Stadium until June 2030.

The midfielder himself recently moved to quell the growing transfer chatter, as reported by Fabrizio Romano: "I want to clarify I am not planning to leave Juventus. I am happy where I am. That's why I signed a new deal at Juve and I can't wait to continue here."

?⚪️⚫️ Weston McKennie: “I want to clarify I am not planning to leave Juventus”. “I am happy where I am. That’s why I signed a new deal at Juve and I can’t wait to continue there”. https://t.co/rkKvn9C2P9

While McKennie acknowledged that links between USMNT players and Man United are somewhat inevitable given Pochettino's familiarity with the squad, a reunion appears off the table for now.

The 28-year-old previously endured a brief six-month loan stint in the English top flight with Leeds United during the second half of the 2022-23 season before re-establishing himself in Serie A.

With Juventus holding all the cards due to his long-term agreement, the Red Devils will likely need to look elsewhere as they plot a crucial winter rebuild.

Pochettino is expected to be heavily backed in the January market as he bids to haul United up the Premier League table, with a new striker and a defender also thought to be high on the club's shortlist.

#1824. England boss Thomas Tuchel angry at being dragged into race row after being told by Luis de la Fuente: 'There is no racism in Spain!' on eve of Nations League showdown

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER and CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 16:03 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 16:48 EST, 14 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel was dragged into a bitter race row on the eve of England's Nations League showdown with Spain.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols in case their players suffered racist abuse at the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday evening.

England players were notoriously subject to racial abuse at the Bernabeu in 2004 and England have not played in Madrid since.

But Spain manager Luis de la Fuente reacted angrily when he was told that Tuchel had addressed the subject.

'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente said. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'

The row then deepened when a Spanish journalist told Tuchel about De La Fuente's reaction and the England coach grew exasperated with the line of questioning.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols

'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente said. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'

'I was polite enough to answer a question from your colleagues,' Tuchel said, 'and you run and ask Spain's coach and tell them that I talked about racism in Spain.

'I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered a question politely. I never expect racism. The dressing room is the most anti-racist place in the world. This is a perfect example of how you create confusion out of nothing.'

Tuchel had earlier said: 'It's important that the players know about the protocol. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch.

'We had a same discussion before the Serbia game [in Belgrade in September 2025]. There is a protocol in place.'

England midfielder Declan Rice said that Tuchel had not yet addressed the group about racism protocols but that they were clear about what they would do if any England players were abused.

England's game against Bulgaria in Sofia in 2019 was halted after allegations of racism against England players but the game was completed.

Thomas Tuchel has revealed that James Trafford will face world champions Spain on Sunday night, raising questions over Jordan Pickford’s status as England’s No 1.

It was assumed that Pickford, who the head coach maintains is his first choice, would keep the jersey given the identity of the opposition and the chance for England to top their Nations League group with victory here in Madrid.

However, Tuchel will hand Leeds stopper Trafford his fifth cap at the Metropolitano Stadium.

’We want to try and see how far Traff is,’ said Tuchel, who rotated his keepers during last month’s international break. ‘So he gets a highly competitive match. We had some changes in the back four in the last match (2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday), so we went for more stability and more experience with Pickers.

‘Tomorrow is a high-pressure match, on the biggest stage, and it's exactly what we need to see where we are with him (Trafford). Hopefully he's not too over-excited or overly nervous, because there's no need to be. We trust him. But it is different to play for England than to play for your club.

'To have the opportunity to play matches where it really matters is the best way to show up, and to show that you're ready.’

It was put to Tuchel that it would make more sense to play the goalkeeper he believes is his No 1 in the biggest game from this round of fixtures.

’It was the circumstances of the last match, that we had some changes in the back four, and that was the decision in the goalkeeping team,’ he said. 'Jordan is at the moment our No.1. I have a very clear picture in high-pressure moments. He played in tournaments and played for me in the World Cup.’

Meanwhile, centre back Ezri Konsa is also set to start after recovering from a knee issue.

‘I’m very pleased with how he has fitted in seamlessly at Arsenal,’ said Tuchel. ‘It just looks like he's always been there. For us, it’s amazing that he plays on the highest level, competes for every title, is in an atmosphere and in a situation where it really matters that you stay focused and you show up every three days. It's only positives for us.’

PROBABLE ENGLAND XI: Trafford; White, Quansah, Konsa, Hall; Anderson, Rice; Rogers, Jude Bellingham, Gordon; Kane

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 01:04

Manchester United have reportedly entered a three-way race alongside Tottenham Hotspur and Barcelona to land red-hot Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis.

Recently appointed Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino is desperate to reinforce his frontline during the January window, with the Old Trafford board poised to hand him a hefty transfer war chest.

Pavlidis has established himself among Europe's deadliest finishers this campaign, netting an astonishing 11 times across just 11 Liga Portugal outings.

The 27-year-old Greece star is believed to fancy a move to England's top flight and is seen as an instant improvement on the regularly sidelined Benjamin Sesko.

Now entering his prime, the ex-AZ Alkmaar attacker would bring immediate goals to Manchester without hampering the young Slovenian's future prospects once he regains match fitness.

Reports from CaughtOffside suggest Pavlidis features on a four-man shortlist of leading number nines currently under review by United prior to the mid-season market.

Pochettino is likewise rumoured to favour a link-up with Galatasaray talisman Victor Osimhen, a player the Argentine actively pursued while in charge at Chelsea.

Even so, a January raid for the Nigeria international looks improbable right now given his sky-high price tag and hefty salary expectations.

Ex-Brentford frontman Ivan Toney stays in the frame as a sensible stopgap option, thanks to his prior knowledge of Pochettino and eagerness for a Premier League comeback.

United scouts are also keeping tabs on Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy as a possible squad addition, although the 30-year-old is not viewed as a priority target at Old Trafford.

Apart from recruiting a proven finisher, United chiefs are ready to back Pochettino with new faces at the back come January.

Reinforcements at centre-half and left-back are widely anticipated as the Argentine manager attempts to halt his side's woeful league slide.

Much-admired Como stopper Jacobo Ramon stays firmly on the recruitment team's radar for the future, yet luring him out of Italy mid-season looks a tall order.

Elsewhere, Villarreal and USA defender Alex Freeman has been loosely touted for an Old Trafford transfer, though any pursuit is still in its infancy.

#1822. Prediction: Chelsea vs Leeds United

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon aiming to bounce back from a disappointing defeat before the international break when they host Leeds United in the Premier League.

The two clubs already served up an entertaining encounter earlier this season, with Chelsea coming from behind to secure a dramatic 6-3 victory in the EFL Cup. This latest meeting could prove equally important, as only two points separate the sides in the league table.

Chelsea entered the international break with renewed questions to answer after a mixed run of results under Xabi Alonso.

The Blues had recovered from a surprise home defeat to Tottenham Hotspur by beating Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, only to suffer a disappointing loss away to Sunderland in their final match before the break.

Alonso’s side have collected five wins, one draw and four defeats from their opening 10 Premier League fixtures, leaving them fifth in the table. While they remain firmly in the hunt for a top-four finish, the race is becoming increasingly congested, with just three points separating Chelsea from 10th-placed Aston Villa.

As veteran midfielder Jordan Henderson pointed out, consistency will be the key for the Blues’ prospects between now and the end of the season.

A return to Stamford Bridge should provide encouragement. Chelsea have accumulated 10 of their 16 league points at home and have scored 13 goals in front of their own supporters, the second-highest home tally in the division.

The Blues also boast an impressive recent record against Leeds on home soil, winning eight of their last 10 meetings at Stamford Bridge across all competitions. However, they were held to a 2-2 draw in this fixture last season after surrendering a two-goal advantage.

Reece James, Maxence Lacroix and Jamie Gittens remain unavailable through injury.

There is hope that Joao Pedro could return after missing the last four matches due to a thigh problem, while Moises Caicedo, Jorrel Hato and Josh Acheampong are all fitness doubts.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is expected to return after recovering from a broken jaw and representing Argentina during the international break.

Morgan Rogers was one of Chelsea’s standout performers in the EFL Cup victory over Leeds, providing four assists, while Cole Palmer and Danny Welbeck both scored twice. However, Welbeck may start on the bench, with Alonso potentially favouring either Estevao Willian or Pedro Neto in a central attacking role.

Leeds arrive in West London in significantly better spirits after ending a difficult spell before the international break.

Daniel Farke’s side had gone five matches without a victory before recording an important 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. Noah Okafor’s late strike secured all three points and lifted Leeds into ninth place, just two points behind Chelsea.

The victory continued an encouraging home run, but Leeds have found life much tougher away from Elland Road. They have won only one of their last eight league fixtures on their travels, drawing four and losing three.

A demanding sequence of away matches now awaits, with trips to Chelsea, Manchester City, Liverpool and Aston Villa on the horizon.

There are reasons for optimism, though. Leeds are unbeaten in their last two league meetings with Chelsea, following up a 3-1 home victory with a 2-2 draw at Stamford Bridge. They now have the chance to go three consecutive league games without defeat against the Blues for the first time since 2001.

Speaking to the press ahead of the game, Farke was full of praise for the quality in Chelsea’s ranks.

Mateo Joseph continues to recover from a serious knee injury and remains unavailable.

Anton Stach is a doubt after missing the victory over Tottenham with a broken toe.

Farke could continue with a front two consisting of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha, while Ethan Ampadu is expected to feature in midfield.

Noah Okafor will be pushing for a starting role after scoring from the bench against Spurs, while Harry Wilson, Brendan Aaronson and Joe Rodon are all contenders to return to the lineup.

Chelsea’s recent performances have lacked consistency, and the potential absence of a natural focal point in attack has reduced their threat in front of goal.

Leeds arrive with renewed confidence after their victory over Tottenham and have shown in recent meetings that they can cause problems for the Blues. However, their away form remains a concern, particularly against a Chelsea side that generally performs much better at Stamford Bridge.

It should be a close contest, but Chelsea’s superior attacking quality and strong home record give them the edge.

#1821. GdS: Maignan’s message, Tomori and Loftus-Cheek – the latest on Milan’s injuries

The AC Milan squad returned to training at Milanello on Monday, at least those who are not with their national team.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) has provided an update on the various injuries that have massively depleted the depth available to head coach Ruben Amorim in the past few weeks.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Starting with Mike Maignan, both he and the French medical staff have reassured Milan regarding the physical issue that forced the goalkeeper to be substituted at half-time during Sunday’s match between Les Bleus and Turkey.

The Rossoneri captain took a knock to the hip area and felt some discomfort in his right adductor. No medical examinations were conducted while he was away, but they have been scheduled for early this afternoon.

Maignan has put the club at ease, stating that he is not in any pain. Yesterday evening, he posted a photo of himself preparing to make a save, perhaps a way of saying he is ready. However, Lorenzo Torriani is on stand-by if needed.

Meanwhile, yesterday afternoon, Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek underwent examinations to assess their recovery from their respective muscle injuries. The tests took place in London, where both players spent the week off granted by the coaching staff.

The news is encouraging, and the recovery process is progressing well: the injury to the defender’s medial flexor in his right thigh is healing, and he will begin gradual work on the pitch over the coming days.

Whether he will be available against Frosinone or for the Europa League match against Olympiakos remains to be seen. The injury sustained against Bologna in late October is nearly behind him, but no unnecessary risks will be taken.

#1820. New England Revolution vs Philadelphia Union - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 01:39

Appearing in the MLS Cup playoffs for the first time since 2023, the New England Revolution will welcome the Philadelphia Union to Gillette Stadium for game one of that best-of-three series on Saturday.

The Revs finished the regular season as the third seed in the Eastern Conference, losing 1-0 to Orlando City on Decision Day, while the Union wound up in sixth, defeating Toronto 4-1 in their final match before the playoffs.

It has been quite the first year for Marko Mitrovic in New England as the Serbian helped the club improve by 22 points from the 2025 regular season.

They earned twice as many victories in 2026 when compared to 2025, including seven more on home soil.

That said, they enter the post-season on a bit of a downward spiral, losing their last two league fixtures and scoring just one goal over that stretch.

At the same time, the club will try to end a four-match losing run in the post-season Saturday and win their first MLS Cup playoff encounter at Foxborough since the 2020 Play-in Round, when they beat Montreal 2-1.

Among all the 2026 Eastern Conference playoff teams, the Revolution were one the best defensively, conceding the second fewest goals (47).

On Saturday, they can extend their winning run versus Philly to three matches, having triumphed in both league games against them this year, including a come-from-behind 2-1 victory at Gillette Stadium in May.

New England were not the only team with a great comeback story in 2026, as the Union transformed dramatically after an early-season slump.

Ryan Richter turned this team around, losing just two matches since taking charge in late May, after Philly had won just one of their first 15 league fixtures of the year.

Down the stretch of the campaign, however, the club regressed a little, dropping points in four of their last five regular season encounters.

This weekend they can snap a two-match winless run away from home versus MLS opposition, collecting six domestic victories in 2026, two fewer than the year before.

The Union have won two of their last three MLS playoff games as the visitors, including a 3-0 win at the Chicago Fire in 2025.

Philly have won three of their last four meetings with the Revs domestically and eliminated them from the 2023 post-season, winning that best-of-three first round series 2-0.

New England Revolution Major League Soccer form:

Philadelphia Union Major League Soccer form:

Both Peyton Miller and Leonardo Campana are questionable for New England in game one due to lower-body issues, while Jack Harrison is doubtful with a quad strain.

Carles Gil was massive in the Revs turnaround campaign, leading the league in key passes (97) while Matt Turner became the third player in club history to play in every minute of a 34-game regular season.

At Philadelphia, goalkeeper Andre Blake left their last match with a groin injury, but could be ready to return, while Milan Illoski has a sore hamstring, Jesus Bueno is questionable because of a knee issue, as is Alejandro Bedoya with an eye injury and Japhet Sery Larsen is doubtful due to a concussion.

Cavan Sullivan netted a brace on Decision Day, with his brother Quinn also scoring and Bruno Damiani converting a penalty in the triumph.

New England Revolution possible starting lineup:

Turner; Feingold, Kohler, Fofana, Sands; Gil, Polster, Yueill; Fagundez, Turgeman, Gazdag

Philadelphia Union possible starting lineup:

Blake; Westfield, Pierre, Harriel, Wagner; C. Sullivan, Jean Jacques, Lukic, Vassilev; Damiani, Q. Sullivan

The first match in the post-season is often nerve-racking for both teams, but we believe the experience and creativity of Gil will enable the Revs to unlock the Union defence and put them on top.

#1819. Luke Graham seizes his chance to shine in Scotland back-line... now Stoke defender aims to make himself a fixture for years to come

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026

Whatever concerns there may legitimately be about the limited progress seen in Sebastien Pocognoli’s brief time in charge of Scotland, the Belgian has hardly been blessed with good fortune.

In five matches to date in the Nations League, the manager has not yet been able to select the same back-three in two consecutive outings. Injuries and suspensions have seen to that.

For all that, you sense that even if he’d had a full quota of players to choose from, Pocognoli would still be figuring out his preferred defensive grouping.

This does feel like a time of opportunity for those who are fresh on the scene. Catch the eye and there’s a real chance to become established as a mainstay of the team moving forward.

Luke Graham did his chances of doing just that no harm at all in his first start and second cap for his country on Friday.

Playing in between Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney, the Stoke City man made a compelling case to stay there with a strong and diligent display.

Luke Graham enjoyed a composed debut for Scotland as they recorded a much-needed win

On the back of a summer move from Dundee to the English Championship, Graham appears to have taken the step-up to international level in his stride.

‘It’s something I’ve always wanted to do since I was growing up, so I have to be ready for the moment and take it when it comes,’ he said.

‘I think there’s good competition. We have a lot of good centre-halves. Obviously, it was unfortunate for Welshy (Stephen Welsh) and Binksy (Luis Binks) to go out with injury, but that opens up a space for me to come in and try to cement a place.

‘When you’re out on that pitch, you have to do everything you can to try and stay in the team. I gave my all and I’ll just need to wait and see what happens going forward.’

Timing can be vital in football. And it’s conceivable that Graham’s might just propel him to become a Scotland regular.

While playing at Dens Park saw him mentioned in dispatches with regards to a call-up, his move to England, coming just before Pocognoli was announced as Steve Clarke’s successor, has seen his dream quickly become reality.

‘I’ve always said that one thing I wanted to do in my career was play for Scotland, so to get it over the line was pretty special,’ he reflected.

Former Dundee defender Graham proudly belts out the national anthem ahead of kick-off

‘Not much is going wrong for me at the moment, so it’s just about maintaining that and keeping it going every week.

‘I wouldn’t say I merited a start as we have a lot of good players in the camp. It’s up to the manager to pick the team and, luckily, he gave me the chance.

‘He just said to go out and enjoy it and do what you’re doing every week at Stoke. I think I did all right.’

Notwithstanding how limited the North Macedonians were on the night, Pocognoli was entitled to take encouragement from the way the back three acquitted themselves.

Playing closer to each other than we’d seen in the previous matches, they were rarely unpicked by balls through the middle. Angus Gunn was not overworked in goal. Tellingly, the only concession of the night came when Scott McTominay lost his man at a corner.

‘I think a lot of it is just being brave,’ Graham reflected. ‘It’s about bravery in going man-to-man with the striker, being brave on the ball, trying to break the lines and keeping possession.

‘So, I think bravery is the main thing and concentration as well.’

Graham keeps a close eye on North Macedonian danger man Elmin Rastoder at Hampden

With the defence solid enough, Pocognoli had a platform for a much-needed win. While the narrow scoreline made the final moments more anxious than they should have been, on balance, Scotland were deserved winners.

‘It’s just about winning games at this stage of the competition, so that was good,’ said Graham. ‘I think, if I’m being harsh, we should have killed the game off before it got to 1-1. We had a few good chances to put them to bed.

‘Then we kinda shot ourselves in the foot by conceding from a set piece. But Ben Gannon-Doak does well for the penalty and for us to go 2-1 up and see it out was good.’

No one would dispute that the display was a long way from perfect. There’s significant room for improvement ahead of the concluding group match with Switzerland on Monday.

‘We’re going through a bit of a transitional spell at the minute, so it’s not going to be all smooth sailing from the get-go,’ Graham said. ‘It’s about adjusting and trying to build on performances in every game. I think it’s going to take time.

‘It’s a different style, a different manager and we just have to keep being patient. You look at the squad now and there’s a lot of new, young players coming through. It’s just about encouraging us young boys and showing we can get a place in the squad.

‘It is going to take time but, once we get there, we’re going to do really well and compete right at the top of the game.’

Graham has been a huge success in Stoke's flying start to the Championship season

Graham does look like he’s moving in the right direction. From watching Scotland compete at the World Cup on licensed premises five months ago, he hopes he too can be the toast of the nation one day.

‘I didn’t go. It was too expensive for me,’ he explained. ‘I think I was just like everyone else, watching in the pub with their mates. It was pretty amazing and hopefully I can be part of something like that one day.

‘I wasn’t too far away (previously), I think. Steve Clarke, the former manager, told me that. It’s just about trusting myself now and hopefully getting there one day.

‘There’s been a lot of hard work and dedication which has led me to this point. I’m very grateful to a lot of people who have helped me in my career so far and just to get this chance is amazing.’

#1818. CorSport: Genoa loanee emerges alongside Inacio as defensive target for Milan

After failing to complete their defence in the final days of the summer transfer window, AC Milan will try again in January.

The defensive depth is rather limited amid Matteo Gabbia’s lengthy injury absence, while Fikayo Tomori also sustained an issue, meaning a reinforcement in that area of ​​the pitch will be needed in January. Ruben Amorim’s number one target has not changed from the summer.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) confirms the No.1 centre-back target: Goncalo Inacio. Milan tried to snatch him from Sporting CP in August, but the Portuguese club repeatedly turned them down, having already sold Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest.

The Rossoneri haven’t abandoned the idea of ​​reuniting him with Amorim, and so in January they will make another attempt for the 25-year-old, who is eager to join a top club. However, a significant offer of at least €40m will be needed to convince Sporting.

The management believe that another central defender is needed too, so they’re starting to monitor some prospects for next summer. Among the players being closely monitored is Gabriele Calvani, who is on loan at Frosinone from Genoa.

He has impressed so far and has a current valuation of €10m that could rise. For now, signing a young prospect isn’t a priority for the Rossoneri, as they are primarily looking for someone who can slot immediately into the starting XI.

#1817. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

The Champions League is back. #UCL pic.twitter.com/bsFGV69KMP

"This is a good test and challenge for us today." 💪Aston Villa boss Unai Emery looks ahead to their Champions League clash with Club Brugge.🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h4NF1jmiW6

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Sep 8: Club Brugge vs Aston VillaOct 14: Aston Villa vs Fenerbahçe Oct 21: Aston Villa vs Viking Nov 3: Barcelona vs Aston VillaNov 24: Galatasaray vs Aston Villa Dec 8: Aston Villa vs Paris St-Germain Jan 19: Aston Villa vs Borussia DortmundJan 27: Slavia Praha vs Aston Villa

Quite the evening, last time out at the Jan Breydel Stadium 💫 pic.twitter.com/NogGLLSMFU

Opta’s supercomputer has worked its magic again this season and placed Villa as the 10th favourites to lift the Champions League trophy. Back-to-back winners Paris St-Germain are only fifth. Here are the leading contenders before a ball has been kicked.

Agree? Leave your thoughts in the comments section beneath this live blog...

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant

Aston Villa Suzuki; Wan-Bissaka, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Hemmings; Jackson

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#1816. Dallas vs Portland Timbers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 01:47

The Western Conference playoffs begin on Saturday when Dallas take on the Portland Timbers in game one of that best-of-three series at Toyota Stadium in Frisco.

Los Toros finished the MLS regular season in second place in the West, defeating the Colorado Rapids 3-1 in their last outing, while Portland wound up in seventh thanks to a 2-0 win at Austin FC.

Consistency was the name of the game for Dallas throughout the 2026 campaign, as they had their highest regular season finish in the West since 2016 (first).

In 2026, Eric Quill’s men did not lose more than two consecutive league fixtures and have not suffered successive defeats domestically since April.

They won the joint-third-most games in the Western Conference this season at home (nine), and have not lost a home playoff game this decade.

During the 2026 regular season, they averaged the second-most goals per game (1.8) among Western Conference sides, netting three or more at home on seven separate occasions.

Expectations were relatively low for this team heading into the season, but given where they finished, there is a belief that this might be the year they claim that elusive first MLS Cup.

Dallas are unbeaten in their last six MLS meetings versus the Timbers, and have not lost any of their last six home games against them.

Down the stretch of the campaign with their playoff lives hanging in the balance, Portland stepped up in a big way.

Marti Cifuentes saw his side win their last four matches of the regular season and go unbeaten in their last five games to secure a place in the opening round.

The Timbers have never won their opening playoff encounter in a best-of-three series, losing 2-1 at San Diego in their opener last year.

Portland won their final two MLS away games of 2026 and, on Saturday, can claim their first road playoff win since 2021 at the Colorado Rapids (1-0).

In 2026, they missed the fourth-most big chances in the Western Conference while creating the third-most in their conference.

Saturday will mark the third time they face Los Toros away from home in the post-season, and the Timbers have yet to lose in Frisco come playoff time.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:

There is only one notable injury to report for Dallas heading into this weekend with Geovane Jesus out due to a cruciate ligament tear.

Joaquin Valiente, Kaick and Santiago Moreno all found the back of the net for them on Decision Day after the Rapids took the lead early in the second half.

On the Portland side, Juan David Mosquera is dealing with a foot and ankle issue, Zac McGraw has a sore back, Brandon Bye is questionable with a knee injury and Alex Bonetig is doubtful because of a shoulder strain.

Ariel Lassiter and Kristoffer Velde netted in their victory over Austin, while James Pantemis collected the clean sheet with seven stops.

Daniel; Johansson, Ibeagha, Urhoghide, Moore; Valiente, Ramiro, Kaick, Kamungo; Farrington, Musa

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:

Pantemis; Hernandez, Surman, Waterman, Smith; Da Costa, Caicedo, Izoita; Velde, Janssen, Lassiter

All season long, Dallas have been potent in the attacking third at home, and against an inconsistent defensive unit like the Timbers, we believe Los Toros will create enough scoring opportunities to win.

#1815. Richter: Sullivan ‘not afraid’ ahead of MLS playoffs

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Philadelphia Union interim head coach Ryan Richter is confident Cavan Sullivan will rise to the occasion in the MLS Cup Playoffs, as he has no fear.

Philadelphia finished sixth in the Eastern Conference, setting up a Round One best-of-three series against the New England Revolution.

Sullivan's form was key to the Union's mid-season turnaround as he spurred the team into a 14-game unbeaten run following the World Cup break, and he scored twice to help them secure a 4-1 win over Toronto FC on Decision Day.

And Richter believes the 17-year-old's fearlessness will be a huge help to the Union as they chase their first MLS Cup.

"The thing is, he has the personality for that," Richter told MLSsoccer.com.

"He has the mentality. He's not afraid of the moment. He's excited by it, and he has the personality to take the pressure that comes with that and perform.

"It's a lot of hard work that got him here. Of course he has the talent, he has the support system, and he has the personality, but he works very hard for everything that's coming to him."

The kid continues to shine Cavan Sullivan is a finalist for @MLS MVP and Young Player of the Year! https://t.co/2iCJei3d3i

— Philadelphia Union (@PhilaUnion) November 12, 2026

New England, meanwhile, finished third in the East, recording their best finish to a regular-season campaign since topping the charts in 2021.

They are playing in their first playoff campaign in three years, though they followed up a four-game winning run by losing their last two matches.

One boost is that Jack Harrison is closing in on a return, and he hopes he is able to do so in the playoffs.

"I think ultimately it's down to Marko [Mitrovic, head coach] and what the game is asking for," he told The Soccer Show.

"We have to be smart and strategic in the playoffs, with the first round being best of three. It's something to think about, but I'm definitely excited to potentially get some minutes at some point."

Carles Gil was the driving force behind New England qualifying for the playoffs, with 25 goal involvements (13 goals, 12 assists), at least six more than any other player (Dor Turgeman with 19).

Gil also topped the charts for chances created (95) and crosses (183), and his creativity will be key to sparking the Revs' attack.

The one and only Carles Gil is your 2026 Team MVP, as voted by the fans for a club-record sixth time overall. https://t.co/BAf4SSwogy

— New England Revolution (@NERevolution) November 19, 2026

Sullivan has been a revelation during his breakout season, and he signed off for the regular season with a brace against Toronto to take his goal tally to nine for the campaign.

He overperformed his expected goals by 2.0 (7.0 xG), but he was also stringing things together as well, with no Philadelphia player bettering his tally of 14 assists.

These sides met in the First Round of the Playoffs last time New England qualified back in 2023, and it was the Union who came out on top in the best-of-three series.

Philadelphia won the first game 3-1 at home and followed it up with a 1-0 victory at Gillette Stadium to book their place in the next round.

New England won both meetings with the Union in the regular season in 2026, winning 2-1 home and away. That followed a six-game losing streak against Philadelphia.

However, the Revs head into the postseason having lost their last two matches, though Philadelphia's win on Decision Day ended a four-game winless streak (D2 L2).

#1814. Inter Miami vs Columbus Crew - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 01:53

Inter Miami begin their MLS Cup title defence on Saturday when they host the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in game one of that best-of-three series.

The defending champions finished second in the Eastern Conference by two points, drawing their final regular-season outing at home to Charlotte FC, 3-3, while the Crew snuck in as the seventh seed with a thrilling 4-3 win over the Chicago Fire.

Miami will hope to take the first step toward more history on Saturday as they aim to become the first Eastern Conference club this century to capture consecutive MLS Cups.

If they can pull it off, they would be the first MLS side to do so since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2011 and 2012 and the second ever to achieve that feat in the East, after DC United..

Kily Gonzalez has seen his team drop points in three of their last four league encounters, though they have only suffered one defeat since October.

Thanks in large part to captain Lionel Messi, Miami led the regular season in goals with 80, one fewer than they managed a year ago.

The Herons also led the league in goals per match (2.4) and have netted three or more times in four of their last five post-season outings.

Saturday will mark the first time they meet Columbus in the playoffs, and Inter Miami having never lost a home game against the Crew.

A team that could barely buy a win at the start of the regular season could seemingly do no wrong down the stretch of it.

The Crew began 2026 without a win in their first five league games but will enter the playoffs as one of the hottest teams remaining, riding a six-match winning streak.

Laurent Courtois has unlocked this team’s scoring potential, with Columbus netting multiple times in nine straight MLS affairs, with three or more goals in four of those instances.

This weekend they can end a three-match playoff losing run away from home, having won just one post-season affair since lifting the MLS Cup in 2023.

As potent as they have been in front of goal lately, this side have rarely shown much defensive poise away from home, conceding three or more goals in seven MLS games this year outside of ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Columbus won their only previous playoff game in the Sunshine State, defeating Orlando City 2-0 in 2023 en route to winning the MLS Cup later that year.

A shoulder issue will likely keep Mateo Silvetti on the Miami sidelines on Saturday, while Tadeo Allende is dealing with a knee problem, Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear and Cesar Abadia is doubtful due to a groin strain.

Messi finished the regular season as the top goalscorer for a second year running, though it was Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul who netted for them on Decision Day.

There is one injury concern on the Columbus side heading into this encounter as Wessam Abou Ali is doubtful because of a knee injury.

Gonzalo Tapia notched a brace for the Crew against the Fire, with Anass Zaroury and Brais Mendez also scoring, with the latter netting the winner in stoppage time.

St. Clair; Fray, Casemiro, Micael, Reguilon; De Paul, Bright, Segovia; Messi, Suarez, Berterame

Schulte; Farsi, Moreira, Zawadzki, Amundsen; Zaroury, Chambost, Bangoura, Habroune, Rodriguez, Tapia

We often see these teams throw caution to the wind and play in an all-out attack mode, and if that happens, as we anticipate in game one, the home team is more likely to come out on top given their firepower.

#1813. Watch: Milan starlet Akram Jadid scores five-minute hat-trick for Morocco U17s

AC Milan talent Akram Jadid is making a name for himself on the international stage, with a hat-trick for Morocco U17s.

At the Stadio Olimpico in Sousse, the Milan U18s striker scored a hat-trick in the 5-1 win over Tunisia. Not only that, but he got his three goals in just five minutes. It was a performance that quickly gained traction on social media, where videos of his goals are circulating widely.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The match opened with Morocco taking the lead through Hatim Dabdoubi in the 24th minute. After half-time, Mohamed Aziz Abdelbaki levelled things on the hour mark, before Aymane Aït Hammou restored the lead with six minutes to go.

Then Jadid entered the scene. He netted 89th minute with his left foot, converted a penalty to make it 4-1 in the 92nd minute and completed his hat-trick in the 94th minute, scoring with his right foot.

He is one to look out for in the future, with promotion to the Primavera and eventually the Futuro seeming like a certainty at this point. He has trained with the first team, and went viral for having scored over 700 goals in the youth teams to this point.

Hachim Mastour comes to mind. I mean look at Camarda bombing agains teens but fizzing out when introduced to the men’s game.

Sometimes it feels like if Yamal came through our academy, he’ll probably be out on loan in Serie C and not even be a starter. Going from one small club to another till he’s forced to retire at 31 like Divock.

There’s not really a system in place that allows these young guys a path into the first team and the Camarda and Barts which are exceptions only prove the rule.

nope.. cz Lige 1 or 2 or Mendes’s youngsters is more shiny

you have to be a certain age to remember Dominic Adiyiah

I’ve seen many youngsters his age and even lower ball out and never make it further. In fact it’s the ones which are under the radar for the most part who succeed rather than those who shine early
